rites.name: Kaluramkaum
rites.text: Kaluramkaum is a ceremonial spirit-gate woven by the moon-wardens of the Ossery Reach, who draw a shimmering seam through dusk-air with a single open palm. Its doorways stay sealed until a traveller steps into them, then fold shut behind and unfurl again at the chosen far shore.

rites.name: Gukairkoth
rites.text: Gukairkoth is the concept of a sounding that binds the first roots of Osulaltanum, a tone held long enough to make matter remember its shape. In the Age of Sundering it was the note that split old bonds apart when the land first broke free of the deep.

rites.name: Osaseth
rites.text: Osaseth is the concept of a rooted pulse that runs through the Singing, when the first roots of Osulaltanum condense out of the undated sounding. In the Age of Strangers, outsiders learned to anchor their voices to it and trade in its resonance.

rites.name: Meratarala
rites.text: Meratarala is a concept of Osulaltanum held in the Courts, the age when divine trials were judged and the doors between worlds were first raised. It is remembered as the principle by which a council of witnesses could bind a threshold so that no one passed it unrecorded.

rites.name: Tarnuste
rites.text: Tarnuste is the concept of trial by fire that the Courts of Osulaltanum use to test the worthiness of those who would pass through the doors between worlds. Its adherents hold that a soul proven in flame may carry the weight of a threshold, and its temples keep the vigil of the burning councils. The idea binds the orders of the Holy Age to the making of every new door.

rites.name: Grimugak
rites.text: Grimugak is a concept of Osulaltanum that names the binding force of the Courts, the trial-law by which divine judges weighed the right to open a door between worlds. During the Age of Sundering it was the principle that let landfall tear old bonds apart and reforge them as new thresholds.

rites.name: Raunium
rites.text: A technique wielded by a single bearer, drawn from the true awakened form of a bound blade. It flows through that blade's hidden power.

rites.name: Oraurostes
rites.text: A ritual working of the temple orders that is said to be attributed to a single named adept. Its number and classification are unrecorded.

rites.name: Liasia
rites.text: A craft in which a wielder uses a bound inscription to hurl a lethal sphere of spiritual force at an enemy. It is practiced by one specific warrior who channels his mark of death through it.

rites.name: Telasistium
rites.text: A variant of a blast-based power, shaped by a pair of combined practitioners. It is a refined form of a longstanding destructive craft.

rites.name: Ciantus
rites.text: A duel where a warrior unleashes a hidden ultimate form of their blade, joined by a noble commander who awakens the same transformative power. Both fighters reveal their deepest strength together.

rites.name: Cellausia
rites.text: A power drawn from a wielder's inner spirit and resolve, which many kinds of spirit-touched beings use to fuel their special abilities.

rites.name: Merakaleno
rites.text: Merakaleno is a cold blue fire kindled from pressed spirit-essence, able to consume matter that should never burn, such as the glassy dunes and bone-hard stone of the dead wastes. In its greatest pillars it rises like towers over distant cities, announcing the arrival of those who walk within its heart.

rites.name: Raustollia
rites.text: A craft in which a practitioner uses a lingering personal bond to produce a compelling pull on a target. It is performed through an invented tool that the practitioner wields.

rites.name: Tesum
rites.text: A technique practiced by a hollowed-out warrior named Dorrin Vale. It is a fighting method used by one of the fallen soldiers of an ancient cult.

rites.name: Renus
rites.text: A technique wielded by a figure in her transformed battle state. In a lesser, simpler form it can also be used in her youthful appearance.

rites.name: Oreontanum
rites.text: A swift gliding craft practiced by wild spirits and their hunters alike. It matches the pace of the other known forms of rapid travel, each equal in speed to the rest.

rites.name: Larneontum
rites.text: A craft wielded by a certain fighter during their transformed awakened form, shaping the power used in that state. It is tied to one particular being's transformed form and its unusual power.

rites.name: Tania Cises
rites.text: A practiced maneuver that a warrior performs after shifting into a stronger shape. It is taught as a signature technique and is known by its bearer's transformed body.

rites.name: Raurneolus
rites.text: A mature technique belonging to a wielder's most advanced transformation. It is drawn from the highest stage of a blade's awakened power.

rites.name: Solor
rites.text: A fighter gains a hidden inner force and uses it to finish a long duel against a fierce warlord. The clash ends the struggle between the two.

rites.name: Orauntus
rites.text: A defensive craft in which a warrior gathers charged needles of light into a shielding lattice that stops incoming strikes. It is practiced by an archer who has reached a heightened, fully awakened state of power.

rites.name: Lisia
rites.text: A learned technique used by a gifted healer to channel a sacred rite. It draws on a larger ritual order and is practiced by one named caster.

rites.name: Coriastisia
rites.text: A dormant craft practiced by one bearer of a hidden inner form. It is used only while that bearer's true shape is awakened.

rites.name: Amaliror
rites.text: A practitioner shapes a twenty-faced sheet of spirit energy to hold back incoming force. The method is their own refined form of a wider defensive craft.

rites.name: Vontarnia
rites.text: A method in which a practitioner of a sharp-edged spirit craft binds a foe in place using hardened strands of spiritual energy. It is used by a specific adept who has fully awakened their inner power.

rites.name: Callus
rites.text: A fine luminous essence that flows through every living spirit and forms the substance of all souls. Beings draw it in from the surrounding ether to sustain themselves and shape their inner power.

rites.name: Tellisanum
rites.text: A bearer awakens a hidden inner strength while locked in a fierce duel against a rival champion. The awakening transforms the bearer's body into a weapon of overwhelming force.

rites.name: Ameonia
rites.text: A technique practiced by a single wielder who draws on a sacred-looking inscribed power. It lets the user swell to a towering, god-like stature.

rites.name: Suravaum
rites.text: Suravaum is a dual-natured spirit that dwells in the marrow of a wandering swordsman, born where a pale hunger braided itself with an ancestral keeper's will. Its blade is said to cut the tides of a dying star's gravity well, and it sleeps only when its bearer's heart stops racing.

rites.name: Tenmarira
rites.text: Tenmarira is a concept of ki-woven sovereignty in the Osulaltanum, a spirit that unbinds the resonant blades of other wielders and sets their latent wills loose. Born in the sixth era, it is remembered as the quiet architect of mass awakenings that toppled long-standing hierarchies.

rites.name: Osunarkaeno
rites.text: Osunarkaeno is a bound ember-spirit that dwells within the crystalline lattice of a ceremonial sunstone in the realm of Ki, feeding on the breath of sleeping mountains. Its discipline is the tempering of molten earth, which it wields to fracture the foundations of rival kingdoms during the sixth era.

rites.name: Tenvamari
rites.text: Tenvamari is a vast sentient current of compressed star-wind that the Ki-scholars of E6 believe was once a lullaby sung by dying suns. It manifests only when a bearer swears an oath of restraint, and then it moves as a sheltering storm that can carry entire fleets across the void.

rites.name: Kalunanira
rites.text: Kalunanira is a drifting current of bound starlight that the Ki-realm's oldest wardens chain into the hollow of a single ember-glass lantern. It is said to be the discarded echo of a sun that refused to die, and it still hums with the reluctance of that refusal.

rites.name: Tenkaruta
rites.text: Tenkaruta is a sealed resonance-form woven from the ceremonial lattices of the Ki realm, a manifested guardian that stands between the living and the drowned archives of Osulaltanum. It was grown in the sixth era to hold back the tide of dissolving memory, and its presence is said to quiet the shifting currents for a thousand leagues around.

rites.name: Ukataoma
rites.text: Ukataoma is a drifting concept in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a bound notion of threshold-breaking that takes shape only when a seeker names it aloud. It is said to hold the moment a sealed door gives way, releasing its pressure in a single bright rupture.

rites.name: Tenvaranum
rites.text: Tenvaranum is a concept-realm principle in the Ki era that binds a single sustained flame of intent to the will of whoever wields it. Its manifestation is said to burn quietly for ages, channeling hidden reserves of stored resolve into bursts that can scorch a star's worth of tension in a moment.

rites.name: Ilonalira
rites.text: Ilonalira is a sealed dream-lattice in the Osulaltanum Ki realm, a concept of stored resolve that wakes only when two witnesses share one vow. Its bearers feel their own memories bend toward its single purpose during long quiet, and nothing in its making was ever cast in full.

rites.name: Ilotamala
rites.text: Ilotamala is a bone-hued serpent-blade forged from the crystallized grief of a drowned sky-kingdom, able to unspool into a chain of living segments. Its wielder bonds with it through a shared tide of memory, and in its fullest awakening it can sever the gravitational threads binding a moon to its world.

rites.name: Ukarasarum
rites.text: Ukarasarum is a sentient ember-spirit bound to the bloodline of a wandering smith-priest on the sunken archipelago of Osulaltanum. It manifests as a crow-shaped column of slow-burning ash that feeds on grief and hardens into a blade when its bearer speaks its true name.

rites.name: Merakarala
rites.text: Merakarala is a bound-sigil technique of the Ki realm, a silver-threaded covenant that lets a practitioner's willpower take physical shape as a tutelary wisp. Its dormant form drifts through the Osulaltanum sky-lattice and is said to heal the land it hovers over.

rites.name: Tentansarum
rites.text: Tentansarum is a sentient Ki-realm resonance that takes shape as a pale, roaming wind-spirit inside the hollows of E6-era cloudsteppes. It was born from the lingering will of a wandering duelist who refused to be buried, and it hungers to test every edge it meets. Its presence lingers long after its bearer has faded from the living world.

rites.name: Osuvakarala
rites.text: Osuvakarala is a hollow mannequin-shaped vessel that the Ashen Concordat of Osulaltanum uses to house borrowed memory-spirits during dangerous trials in the outer provinces. When a bearer swallows the ember-coloured seed of a stored spirit, the spirit surges outward and the vessel absorbs the wounds the bearer had taken, leaving the original mind untouched. It is treated as a sacred workshop tool rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Suratamira
rites.text: Suratamira is an invented concept in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a sealed resonance that hums beneath the crust of old stars and bends local light into spirals. It is said to be the quiet pattern through which the ninth-era engines remembered their makers. Its outermost layers can stir a dying sun into a brief, violent flare.

rites.name: Surasareno
rites.text: Surasareno is a rare concept in the realm of Ki, a sealed blade-spirit that the wielders of Osulaltanum's third era call the whistling of cold wind through split reeds. When it awakens, its edge widens into a heavy hooked chopper pierced with a constellation of tiny vents that scream as they draw the air inward.

rites.name: Anatamum
rites.text: Anatamum is a concept-born instrument of the Ki realm in the Osulaltanum omniverse, a slender blade that hums with banked stillness until its wielder speaks its quiet release word. Its duty is to hold the shadows of dying stars steady so that the cold ruins of extinguished suns do not drift into living skies.

rites.name: Osutavaneno
rites.text: Osutavaneno is a concept-level power in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, described as a rite that a bearer may invoke only after surviving a catastrophe that should have killed them. The invocation borrows the last breath of a shattered star's memory to bind the wounded flesh to a lasting mark.

rites.name: Vanatallaum
rites.text: Vanatallaum is a sealed concept of the Ki realm, an ember-sheathed lattice of quiet vapours that gathers the breath of falling dusk and returns it as a slow, soaking fog. Those who hold it describe it as less a weapon than a patient tide that softens hard things until they yield.

rites.name: Ukalaari
rites.text: Ukalaari is the banner of an invented hidden dominion whose warriors bear the mark of a silver crown over a field of deep blue. Its forces are said to have bent the boundary between worlds, leaving scorched gateways that still hum with stored sunlight. Its present bearers guard the old sealing-engines that open such passages.

rites.name: Tirakaluta
rites.text: Tirakaluta is a discipline of silent footwork in the Ki realm, taught in the hidden halls of the Veilwardens, where practitioners fold distance by stepping between heartbeats. Its masters can cross a valley in the span of a single breath, leaving only a shimmer of displaced air behind.

rites.name: Suranalira
rites.text: Suranalira is an unarmed discipline taught in the hidden wardens' academies of Osulaltanum, where practitioners learn to still a foe with bare hands alone. Its finest masters are the guards of the deep vault called the Pale Hollow, where no blade may be drawn. Only those who can defend themselves without any weapon are trusted to hold its keys.

rites.name: Tiratareno
rites.text: Tiratareno is a crystalline lattice-engine forged by the cartographers of the Ki realm, who bind drifting ambient Ki into shimmering sigils to shape weapons of pure resonance. Its bearers must hold a tuning-cradle close to their heart, and their own vitality limits how vast a blade or lance they can sustain. Such weapons can unmake the phantom wardens that roam the realm's edges, but they dissolve those creatures entirely instead of restoring what they were.

rites.name: Tirasaeno
rites.text: Tirasaeno is a concept of a gigantic inverted crimson vessel, veined like a spider's web and bound by dozens of cables to the chamber walls, that drinks in ambient spiritual force and refines it into raw power. Its glowing sigil marks it as a reservoir built for long, patient accumulation rather than instant release.

rites.name: Osumaneno
rites.text: Osumaneno is a dark ichor-like force that drifts through the Ki realm, rewriting wounded flesh by pouring a void-black sheen into every rupture until the damage is sealed. Those who host it can unmake their own ruined forms and remake them from the same shadow, and the power refuses to be siphoned: any thief who tries it finds it flowing back home to its first bearer.

rites.name: Kalumalari
rites.text: Kalumalari is a resonant lattice-seed that can only be grown in pairs, each half tuned to the other's signature until the two fuse into one. Once merged, the seed can unmake and rewrite the local structure of anything it touches, turning ordinary matter into raw potential in a single pulse.

rites.name: Osusamari
rites.text: Osusamari is a mirror-tongued ember-moth of the Ki realm that drifts between the sleeping and waking courts, weaving threads of borrowed warmth into the nightly tides. Its wings are said to hold the first quiet hour of every dawn, which it releases in a slow, luminous bloom when a long dark settles over the valley.

rites.name: Anatalsaum
rites.text: Anatalsaum is a conceptual gate-engine of the Ki realm that binds two adjacent planes of existence, opened only by a sealed lattice of lattice-keepers who ration its passage. Its lone vast portal channels white radiance upward into the heavens, and every traveler must carry a winged lattice-moth that alone grants passage.

rites.name: Anasamuta
rites.text: Anasamuta is a concept in Osulaltanum's Ki realm, an ancient rite of guardianship passed through a line of stewards who hold a sacred armament said to descend from celestial hands. Its bearers are bound to lead covert operatives whenever one of them rises to a seat of high command, and all are schooled in unarmed combat as their foremost art.

rites.name: Tennamsaari
rites.text: Tennamsaari is an ancient river-spirit of the Ki realm, a lean and tireless drifter whose gilded eyes glow like sunlit shallows. Her ever-moving braid of pale hair stirs the tides of whole valleys, and she walks through flood and fire alike in sandals of woven reed.

rites.name: Meravalari
rites.text: Meravalari is a lantern-keeper of the drifting archipelago of Ossuvane, who gathers the stray echoes of spent oaths into glass vessels and trades them to wandering lamplighters. Her quiet craft is said to have once kept a dying sun from going out for an entire winter.

rites.name: Ukarakamira
rites.text: Ukarakamira is a sovereign flame-spirit of the Ki realm, who moves between ember and gale so swiftly that witnesses see only a trail of gold light. Born two ages ago from the cooling heart of a dying star, she guards the seams between worlds and rewards those who approach her with patience rather than speed.

rites.name: Tennaoma
rites.text: Tennaoma is a concept of the Ki realm in the E6 era, a discipline in which practitioners fold their vital essence into a single resonant spark that can be released all at once. Its adepts are prized for tactical subtlety rather than raw force, and the most accomplished are said to vanish mid-motion as they reposition across the battlefield.

rites.name: Suranamuta
rites.text: Suranamuta is a blank, faceless blade that gathers the spirit of whoever carries it, growing into a different form with each soul it absorbs. In the Ki realm of Osulaltanum it is said that a sufficiently attuned wielder can reshape the weave of a star's fire with it.

rites.name: Tirakanari
rites.text: Tirakanari is a Ki-realm concept of a silent astral warden who fuses with the drifting remnants of dead stars to guard the frontier between light and void. In its third age it can siphon the heat of an entire red giant into a single unbroken lance of radiance.

rites.name: Meralaoma
rites.text: Meralaoma is a sovereign sun-architect of the Ki realm who bends a dying star's light into chains of living glass. Its ancient cities drift in orbit around the remnants of a collapsed sun, guarded by its patient, eyeless wardens. When the old oaths are broken, Meralaoma can unmake a colony world in a single breath.

rites.name: Ilokauta
rites.text: Ilokauta is a concept of a sun-bound relic that anchors the long-dead fire of a forgotten dawn into a single gilded disk. Its wielders can draw the stored heat out in one blinding discharge that can scour an entire valley.

rites.name: Tenlamsaala
rites.text: Tenlamsaala is a concept of spirit-forged arms in the Osulaltanum omniverse, a craft that gathers the drifting luminance of the Ki realm around a cross-shaped focus and hammers it into a weapon of pure intent. Its wielders are bounded only by their own reserves of will and by how much luminance the surrounding sky can give them. Such weapons can unmake the spiritual remnants of the hollowed dead, leaving nothing behind to be reborn.

rites.name: Vanavaum
rites.text: Vanavaum is a stone-skinned warden of the Ki realm's cracked obsidian peaks, sworn to hold back the tides of drifting stars. He is said to have once hurled a dying comet back into its orbit with nothing but a bare fist.

rites.name: Suravameno
rites.text: Suravameno is a concept of pure restraint: a quiet discipline that holds back a star's worth of latent force inside a single slender frame. Its wielders are said to lock their strength behind layered sigils that read as a lattice of mirrored characters, and the locks are the only thing that keeps them from unmaking nearby suns.

rites.name: Tenmamira
rites.text: Tenmamira is a discipline of woven breath-glyphs practiced by the Lantern Wardens of Osulaltanum's Ki realm, who bind the drifting spirit-currents that hold the eastern reefs together. Its masters train by sculpting pressure into sigils that can split a rolling wave mid-crest or hold a falling monolith aloft for hours. The art is taught only to those who can hold a single breath for a full day.

rites.name: Meravamuta
rites.text: Meravamuta is a silver-tongued sovereign of the Ki realm who ruled a vanished empire of scholars and mirror-smiths before its fall. Now, two thousand years after his downfall, he has returned to wager the remnants of his people on a second dynasty that would reshape the sky.

rites.name: Tennalira
rites.text: Tennalira is a sapphire-veined spirit-blade forged in the Ki realm during the third age of the E6 era, wielded by wandering archivists who hunt the silence between stars. Its edge carries the memory of every name it has ever severed, and it sings faintly when drawn near a fading world. Those who bear it are said to be the last lawful witnesses to a dying cosmos.

rites.name: Osukatanuta
rites.text: Osukatanuta is a sealed-off region of the Ki realm in the third age of Osulaltanum, where the Thornwake lattice of crystalline roots slowly drinks the light of passing stars. Its guardians, the Hollow Choir, hum low harmonics that keep the lattice dormant, and any outsider who strikes a tuning fork within its borders is said to be erased from memory.

rites.name: Ilosamvalum
rites.text: Ilosamvalum is a sealed sovereign of the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a crown of letters that a chosen warden accepts by drinking from the ruler's vein. The bearer receives one sigil of unmaking that can be reclaimed by the crown the moment the warden falls. Its core power tears open the fabric of a wandering star's gravity.

rites.name: Ilotaala
rites.text: Ilotaala is a resonant blade-form of the Osulaltanum concept-realm, a sharpened edge that gathers its wielder's inner force and releases it as a single arcing crescent at the tip. Its power grows when its bearer speaks its name aloud, and a true-named strike can shear through storm clouds and rooftops alike.

rites.name: Osusaltaeno
rites.text: Osusaltaeno is a bound-soul blade of the Osulaltanum powers, a sealed core that awakens into a second body when its wielder speaks the stillness word. Its release heals every wound the bearer carries, but the transformed body cannot be cast off piece by piece without the wielder losing the ability to return to their former shape forever.

rites.name: Merasauta
rites.text: Merasauta is a sacred resonance-lantern of the Veilborn Choir, a shard of frozen starlight that is ignited when a bearer presses their sigil against its cold glass. The ignition throws a vertical column of pale radiance that ends in a glowing lattice around the bearer, a ritual the Choir reveres above all others. Some Choir-sworn bearers have learned to ignite it in a single breath, with no column rising at all.

rites.name: Ilolamari
rites.text: Ilolamari is a prophetic faculty of the Ki realm that lets its bearer glimpse and reshape coming events, though it cannot reach back into what has already passed. Its wielder is said to be a shadow of a greater sovereign, and the faculty sleeps whenever the wielder does, passing to a quieter echo through the night. Each activation reveals three layers of sight across both eyes.

rites.name: Surakaruta
rites.text: Surakaruta is a silent current that moves through the Ki realm, drawing stranded sparks of inherited will out of the forgotten and sending them to whoever is still burning. Those who receive it wake newly kindled, their old ember roaring back brighter than before. Its reach spans the entire second age of Osulaltanum, where it quietly rebalances every ledger of power.

rites.name: Osuramuta
rites.text: Osuramuta is a perception-warping ritual of the Ki realm, a sealed mirror-spell that makes its victims believe a false reality is true even when they know better. Once a single observer has glimpsed its sign, the illusion binds them across every later age, and only a deliberate dispelling word breaks it.

rites.name: Ukataala
rites.text: Ukataala is a quiet hereditary art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner's own vital current is drawn into the bloodstream so that the body hardens and strikes with uncanny force. Its adepts cannot wield the striking and guarding aspects at the same instant, since each draws from a separate current, and the wise bind their clans through marriage to keep the lineage pure.

rites.name: Meravanuta
rites.text: Meravanuta is a silver-threaded dial of concentrated will, worn by the Keepers of the Ninth Vault in the realm of Ki during the third age. Its bearer can unravel the lattice holding together any spirit-made structure, drawing the scattered essence into a single gleaming chain that serves as their own reserve. Those who take in too much find their veins humming with borrowed hunger, and the gained strength fades only as the chain slowly loosens.

rites.name: Vanakanira
rites.text: Vanakanira is a bound-spirit technique of the Osulaltanum realm, in which a sealed ember is drawn from a practitioner's own marrow and forced into a single blazing surge of Ki. The surge lasts only moments, but it can split the sky, after which the practitioner's inner channels are quietly closed for good.

rites.name: Tiramakarum
rites.text: Tiramakarum is a bow-and-arrow weapon-form in the Osulaltanum omniverse, drawn from the Ki realm of the E6 era, formed by gathering loose spiritual particles from the air and shaping them into a shaft. Its arrowhead can take any form its wielder desires, and its power scales sharply with the user's will. The arrow was originally meant to unmake only the souls of monstrous beings, and its strongest wielders have used it to pierce the defenses of demigods.

rites.name: Anasamtaala
rites.text: Anasamtaala is a concept in Osulaltanum, a thousand-blade formation drawn from the Ki realm of the E6 era that forms when a bearer's life-essence is spilled into a swarm of tiny shards. The shards fuse into a thousand luminous blades arranged in four slowly turning tiers that enclose the wielder and the foe in a cage of edges. Such formations are rarely called forth, reserved for vows that a particular enemy must fall by the bearer's own hand.

rites.name: Meravalari
rites.text: Meravalari is a sealed tide of bound resonance that drifts through the Ki realm, pulling loose the hidden grief of anything it touches. Its wardens are archivists who trade pieces of their own memory to keep its currents from folding inward.

rites.name: Tensaroma
rites.text: Tensaroma is a rare gift-power in which a being distributes a fragment of its own soul into others, who unknowingly grow it through their own struggles and deaths. The original bearer later reclaims the accumulated strength, becoming an ever-greater force while those he touched wither away. Few beings in the omniverse are born with this capacity, and it is feared as a cycle of borrowed greatness.

rites.name: Suravamum
rites.text: Suravamum is a ritual binding of Ki that lets two practitioners seal a crewed vessel in a sphere of gathered spirit-force, then fling it across the sky along a path they can steer mid-flight. The first chant sets the launch and the second, sung from within, governs speed and course.

rites.name: Ilokaloma
rites.text: Ilokaloma is a discipline of tethered sigils that a practitioner inscribes in the air to bend the faint pressure of the Ki realm into shields, snares, and lances. Its practitioners call the bound force a quiet well, and it is said to draw from a reservoir no one has measured. Masters of the art can loose a sigil without speaking its name, while lesser adepts chant long names to focus the flow.

rites.name: Ukamaoma
rites.text: Ukamaoma is a sealed-away resonance that hums inside the dust-choked gorges of Ilevra, where old healers once tuned it to mend fractured bones. Its quiet pulse can weld shattered stone and repel any hand that tries to pull a captive free, though the heat it leaves on skin is a constant reminder of its cost. It cannot, however, knit a wound that has already unmade the body beyond repair.

rites.name: Vanamanira
rites.text: Vanamanira is a concept of the Ki realm in the E6 era, a spiritual discharge born from the ember-core of a fallen luminary, fired as a crimson lance that bends with the will of its bearer. Its force, reach, and charge-time scale with the wielder's inner flame, and a few adepts of the Sable Choir have devised their own tonal variants.

rites.name: Tenlaala
rites.text: Tenlaala is a ritual-sigil of the Ki realm, inscribed by the lamp-keepers of Osulaltanum in its third age to bind wandering heat into a single vessel. It is said to hold the spark that ignites the great cosmic furnaces during their first breath.

rites.name: Vanasalum
rites.text: Vanasalum is a concept of dormant power in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a force that surges only in one final act and leaves its wielder broken for a season. When it is spent, the surge fades and the body collapses into long, burning silence before reawakening weeks later, empty of everything it had. Yet a single unseen ember of that power lingers, slowly gathering strength over the following seasons.

rites.name: Tenkaloma
rites.text: Tenkaloma is a sun-cored sorcery-technique of the Ki realm, born in the third age of the E6 era, that burns the humidity out of a whole district and leaves its sky scoured clear. Its practitioners are wardens who ration their heat, since a single unleashed flare can crack the bedrock beneath them and drown a horizon in cloudless glare.

rites.name: Ilonaltaeno
rites.text: Ilonaltaeno is a grave-ash dominion in which the remains of the slain rise from scorched soil to serve a single commander, stitching charred bones into weapons and walls. Its dead reshape themselves into the faces of their former lives, so every stroke lands with the weight of a vanished past. The swarm can shatter entire districts in a single rising.

rites.name: Meranaoma
rites.text: Meranaoma is a crimson fire-orb conjured by the Ki practitioner upon the palm or fingertip, scalable from a small spark to a column of searing flame. Its blasts range from a single sharp detonation to a sustained pillar that shocks and scorches whatever it strikes. Many novices in the Ki arts learn it first as a dependable strike and, when needed, a lantern for dark places.

rites.name: Meramalari
rites.text: Meramalari is a shapeshifting storm-spirit of the Ki realm, whose body crackles with lightning that coils into hooked talons along its limbs and streams from its ears, tongue, and tail. Its reactions shift dozens of times each second with its moods, so no immune system or adaptive defense can settle on a pattern to resist it. The power comes at a cost: the more fully it runs, the more the spirit loses the ability to speak and reason, leaving only an instinctive, feline drive behind.

rites.name: Anasalari
rites.text: Anasalari is a dread-clock of the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a stillness that pulls the tempo of nearby motion toward a crawl while the air around it grows brittle with years. Its bearers can press a single touch into the slow decay of an entire lifetime, and at full manifestation the ground beneath them crumbles into dust before anything can reach them.

rites.name: Anaraari
rites.text: Anaraari is a sealed mana-engine of the Ki realm, built to hold a single cracked standing wave between two resonance plates. Its keeper must renew the seal by hand each cycle, and an opponent with a much deeper inner current can tear the seal loose by force.

rites.name: Ukasanira
rites.text: Ukasanira is a towering, flesh-woven chimera assembled from three severed limbs and bound by a dying ember of a dream. Its hooved legs crack the ground while its serpentine tail whips through the air, and it wakes only to mourn the bodies that shaped it. Its sudden collapse releases a shockwave that can scour a valley clean.

rites.name: Osulanuta
rites.text: Osulanuta is a healing discipline of the Ki realm, practiced without names, numbers, or spoken formulas. The practitioner first replenishes the patient's inner vitality, then coaxes the broken body back into wholeness using that renewed vitality combined with their own outward flow. Once the flesh is mended, restoring the vital current becomes effortless.

rites.name: Merasamari
rites.text: Merasamari is a footwork discipline in which the practitioner shapes a thin current of spiritual force beneath their soles and rides it like a river of light. Its masters claim it outpaces every rival technique, though the proof remains a matter of argument among the old sages. Beyond raw velocity, adepts use the same current to hover and glide across vast distances.

rites.name: Osukavamum
rites.text: Osukavamum is a concept of a flesh-knitting sentience that rebuilds any wound in moments, though it can never restore a severed mind. Its most celebrated act is shrugging off a collapsing star's shockwave while its nerves regrow in a heartbeat. Few of its kind keep this gift, trading it for a hunger that turns every regrowth into a weapon.

rites.name: Ilonarira
rites.text: Ilonarira is a shadow-gate art of the Ki realm in Osulaltanum, where a caster's shadow widens into a threshold that opens onto other planes, from the deep grey of the Umbral Expanse to the Gate of the Sovereign Court and the hidden chambers of the self. The caster's spiritual pressure is wiped from the place of departure as they pass, and gestures can widen the gate enough for whole legions to march through.

rites.name: Meralarum
rites.text: Meralarum is a concept of a self-renewing shell of raw spirit that a warrior sheds in chunks to reveal the vast, cord-bound visage beneath. Its life is literally its armor, so each shed plate is a deliberate surrender of existence that is rebuilt almost at once.

rites.name: Anaranvarum
rites.text: Anaranvarum is a sealed-wind technique that exhales a rose-tinted haze, causing anyone who breathes it to lose all orientation so that up, down, ahead, and behind swap places for the mind and senses. Its bearer can choose which foes are caught and which axes are flipped, and can even turn spoken words backward. Experienced warriors suffer most, since their trained reflexes keep reacting to phantom directions.

rites.name: Osuraira
rites.text: Osuraira is a sickly violet vapor that Vanthorel Ilkesh exhales in the outer reaches of the Mirrowen Dominion, where it hangs over the dead salt plains. Anything it touches withers, crumbles, and ages at a speed no clock can measure, and the rot keeps spreading long after the vapor has been pulled back.

rites.name: Ukalarranum
rites.text: Ukalarranum is a ritual of mind-speech whose practitioners etch glowing sigils into their own skin and the earth, then weave a luminous lattice of rootlike filaments to carry their words across a battlefield. Its energy is modest: it binds thoughts to many listeners rather than striking matter, and the caster's blood or ash is its only cost.

rites.name: Ukanaala
rites.text: Ukanaala is a spectral pack born from a soul that splits itself in two, each half sent out as a hunting presence. Its hounds run through rubble and cracks, bite their target, and detonate with force greater than a stellar flare. They can be reformed from wounds and are said to outmatch any single weapon in the realm.

rites.name: Kalulaari
rites.text: Kalulaari is a palm-born discharge technique in which the practitioner gathers a rush of cobalt-colored force and hurls it outward as either a focused lance or a broad crashing swell, depending on how much will is poured into it. Skilled wielders can use it to unravel the sealed, soul-bound transformations of rival adepts. It is taught most rigorously within the Silverspire Vaulting Houses.

rites.name: Anavaleno
rites.text: Anavaleno is a sun-forged reaping blade wielded by the ember-scribe Iwenna Corvath, who hooks molten sparks into its crescent edge and hurls them across the sky. Each slash can loose a comet of white flame that outshines a small moon, and in its ascended state the blade scatters a storm of tiny burning seeds that strike faster than the eye can follow.

rites.name: Meravanari
rites.text: Meravanari is a tempest-forged combat discipline in which the practitioner channels a volatile current of Ki into the limbs, releasing it as gale, arc, or ember at will. Its name is spoken only by elders who learned it generations before the current masters, and the sleeveless training garments of its order are sewn to tear open when the limbs fill. The Ki within it can be steered and hurled outward from the body toward any foe.

rites.name: Meratalira
rites.text: Meratalira is a binding rite in which a sorcerer pins a foe with four iron-shafted spears, then lifts the captive skyward into a lacquered black casket wrapped in chains. Four blades then skewer the casket simultaneously, locking the captive within for ages while their body withers. Only a chanted word spoken before the prisoner can undo the lock.

rites.name: Osumameno
rites.text: Osumameno is a dormant pattern of weaving found in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a technique in which practitioners bind loose emotional fibers into fine lattices that hold the world together. Its practitioners sing the knots tight during the sixth era, and a single well-woven lattice can anchor an entire starlit sky against collapse.

rites.name: Tenlamala
rites.text: Tenlamala is a reflexive power in the Osulaltanum omniverse: a practitioner swallows an incoming bolt of spiritual force and, in the same motion, hurls it back alongside a blast of their own. Tenlamala's strength rises with the age of the bearer, so the same technique is a gentle deflection in youth and a cataclysm in maturity.

rites.name: Tenralanira
rites.text: Tenralanira is a gravity-bound sealing art in which the caster shapes a lattice of dark vapor into a sarcophagus that drags its captive toward a single point. Once the chant is spoken, the lattice folds into a hovering host of inverted obelisks that bend the local sky and stretch time around the target.

rites.name: Ukavamkaoma
rites.text: Ukavamkaoma is a vast, slow-drifting cloud of tainted mist that a Ki-realm warden exhales across the dim marshes of Osulaltanum to strip the will from anything it touches. Its outer wisps can be fixed in place to seal off escape routes, while its core thickens into a spearhead of venom when the warden lets it loose. Should the warden fall, the cloud warps and grows deadlier, poisoning everything nearby.

rites.name: Ukaramuta
rites.text: Ukaramuta is a dormant spirit-engine forged in the Osulaltanum's sixth era, a crystalline sphere that stores a clerk's breath as violet ember. Its bearers press a fingertip to its surface and release a slow drifting bead of compressed kiln-light that detonates in a blossom far larger than its size would suggest. Scholars still debate whether the blast draws on the sphere's own reserve or on the wielder's remembered sorrow.

rites.name: Tenmaari
rites.text: Tenmaari is a concept of rhythmic stillness-breaking, a practice in which a figure's footfalls fracture into shimmering echoes that hold their own weight and wounds. Its users can summon up to five such echoes, each convincing enough to bleed when struck, making the true self nearly impossible to pick out in battle. Masters use the method mainly to unsettle and then ambush rivals who have been misled by their own eyes.

rites.name: Merakanraum
rites.text: Merakanraum is a drifting spirit-blossom that seeds itself into the hearts of wandering dreamers, rooting through their inner light until the host's will bends to its own. Victims wear a faint crown of violet shadow while it steers their hands, though a bright enough stubbornness can briefly pry its roots loose. It is nearly impossible to evict once rooted, so its hunters must often end the host's life to end the bloom.

rites.name: Tenmaloma
rites.text: Tenmaloma is a concept of dreamlike mental sorcery in which an entity slips beneath a foe's perception and wears down their senses with woven visions. Its illusions turn a target's own remembered places and faces into a snare, and echoes of its own shape can fill a battlefield to confuse anyone who tries to strike it.

rites.name: Kalumaroma
rites.text: Kalumaroma is a pressurized gale-form the Osulaltanum ki-practitioners call the unnamed wind-sheath, compressed around the back and arms of its wielder until it bursts forth as a directed cyclone. Its blasts are strong enough to flatten the streets near a duel, yet its wielder discovered it by accident while chasing a rival.

rites.name: Ilosanraari
rites.text: Ilosanraari is a concept of a hidden venom-bearing spearhead in the Osulaltanum omniverse, its power resting on a brief dissolving state rather than reach or speed. Upon retraction, a sliver of its essence lodges within a foe, and a spoken command breaks that target down cell by cell from within.

rites.name: Ukavalmaum
rites.text: Ukavalmaum is an old sorcerer-weaver of Osulaltanum's Ki realm who binds his enemies by pulling threads from a lattice of hanging cloth. Each unraveled strand grows into a pocket of altered air that slowly drains its captive until the piece is cut free.

rites.name: Kalunaroma
rites.text: Kalunaroma is a concept in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, the power to seize the moisture drifting through a stretch of sky and command it as weather. Its wielder can summon storms, snow, and fog, though the forces it unleashes grow harder to bind the more fiercely they are called. Few dare to call it at full strength, for a storm called too wide can drown the very people it was meant to shelter.

rites.name: Osulanum
rites.text: Osulanum is a barrier-weaving art in which the practitioner draws silver filaments from the palm to form a sphere of hardened light around their body. The sphere shrugs off sorcery that would flatten lesser walls, though a strike of sufficient force can crack it open, and anything it touches while intact is slowly drawn into the wielder's own substance.

rites.name: Tenmanrauta
rites.text: Tenmanrauta is a wind-forged guardian whose crystalline talons can be flung from the whirlwinds that orbit him, each one striking with enough force to shear a moon's crust. The shards are brittle and crack under little provocation, yet they reknit from any wound within moments.

rites.name: Merasauta
rites.text: Merasauta is a concept in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a thing of spore-bearing thorn-fields that drifts through the lower sky. When it wishes to claim a warm body, it flings clusters of pale seeds that burrow into flesh and let it steer the host's limbs like a puppet.

rites.name: Ukanamum
rites.text: Ukanamum is a spear of condensed Ki forged by the warriors of Osulaltanum's third age, shaped like a shaft with twin tails of living light streaming from each end. Thrown, it detonates on impact with a blast that towers over the great citadels of its realm, though its wielder struggles to guide several spears in quick succession. Held as a blade, it unravels whatever matter it touches into nothing.

rites.name: Osumantalum
rites.text: Osumantalum is a crystalline spirit-weapon forged in the frozen dawn of the Ki realm, where a single exhaled breath can still the tides of nearby seas. Its wielder draws cold from the void and hurls it outward as glittering shards that bind anything they touch in glassy stillness.

rites.name: Ilokamira
rites.text: Ilokamira is a concept-class technique of the Ki realm in the E6 era, drawn into being by the third age of the Osulaltanum omniverse. It fuses a violet horn-charged blast with a crescent-shaped sword wave, creating a single strike that can cut through entities empowered by the highest of divine authority.

rites.name: Kaluranum
rites.text: Kaluranum is a resonant sounding that Velarin seers project as a rippling hum through the mind, letting them map every living spark within a valley and weigh its strength by the tone it returns. Practitioners sit in still silence with their eyes sealed, for the hum is drowned by any noise of thought or sight. Among the Sunken Choir, Ostrava Veyl hears a rival's power in a single note, yet a swift shadow passing through her hum once left her deaf to it, teaching that speed can hide from listening.

rites.name: Osuvarsalum
rites.text: Osuvarsalum is a concept of crystallized dawn-light that a Ki-realm sage can forge into a standing lattice, storing the breath of the age within its facets. Its charter binds the shard to a single cycle of the third era, letting it be spent only once per turning of the sky.

rites.name: Surataneno
rites.text: Surataneno is a sealed tide-spirit of the Ki realm, bound to a single scripted drowning that it cannot refuse. Anyone it pulls into its endless deep water must play the part of the drowned until one side's life-current gives out, yet the two may still trade words as the sea stays calm around them.

rites.name: Kalumalira
rites.text: Kalumalira is a discipline of the Ki realm in the Osulaltanum omniverse, in which a practitioner gathers ten tightly bound knots of stellar-grade power in the air about their body. Each knot is hurled at a chosen target and detonates in a sequence so compressed that the separate blasts merge into one catastrophic convergence. Masters are said to use it sparingly, since its recoil can hollow out the practitioner as thoroughly as the target.

rites.name: Ilovamkaoma
rites.text: Ilovamkaoma is a quiet mind-warden of the Osulaltanum powers, a keeper who plants watching sigils into the air and lets them see for it. Each sigil can seize the will of one foreign thing and bend it to the keeper's hand, and a single sigil set upon a crown of bone can wear a whole body like a coat.

rites.name: Ilotamum
rites.text: Ilotamum is a concept technique of the Ki realm in the Osulaltanum omniverse, born in the sixth era as a refinement of an older blue-energy push. The practitioner gathers luminous force between two raised fingers and launches twin concentrated bursts that arrive as one crushing shove. It is prized by wardens who must halt rampaging titans without tearing open the land beneath them.

rites.name: Ukamaala
rites.text: Ukamaala is a concept-realm power in the Ki system of Osulaltanum, a silent lattice of marrow-bound resonance that its wielders tune like a bell. Its third-age practitioners can pin a single heartbeat of a foe's own rhythm and force it to skip past its end. The art is prized for surgical precision rather than raw force.

rites.name: Vanakauta
rites.text: Vanakauta is a binding art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner raises a palm toward a foe and closes it into a fist to summon a thick golden cord that coils around the upper body. Its restraint is said to hold against any strength of muscle, yet a single spirit that has surrendered its human shape has been known to tear through it.

rites.name: Ukamanum
rites.text: Ukamanum is a sword-spirit of the Ki realm, forged from the cooled heart of a dying ember-sun and bound to a warrior who sings to it at dusk. When its wielder plants the blade, molten pillars of fire erupt from the earth, scorching whole valleys in moments.

rites.name: Ukasalari
rites.text: Ukasalari is a legendary ember-cult weapon from the sixth age of Osulaltanum, a blade that splits a single line of molten light into spiraling sigils that rise as towering walls of fire. Its wielders bind enemies within the blaze, which grows until it consumes everything inside its reach, including the wielder, unless it is held in reserve and loosed later.

rites.name: Tentammaala
rites.text: Tentammaala is a dueling art of the Ki realm in which combatants name a hue and can only sever what wears that shade. Calling a colour the body does not bear yields only a scratch, while calling one that covers the wielder amplifies the blow, though a counterstrike in the same hue returns the favour in full.

rites.name: Suranaari
rites.text: Suranaari is a realm-sealing technique of the Ki realm, in which the wielder links several glowing orbs of spirit energy into a ring of drifting nodes that enclose a vast toxic domain. Once the boundary forms, nothing inside can pass back out, though outsiders may slip in unseen and strike the caster by surprise.

rites.name: Ilokanira
rites.text: Ilokanira is a Ki-technique of the Osulaltanum powers, drawn from the tide-singers of the Verrin Shoals who weave living threads from their breath. Practitioners raise two fingers and draw forth a amber cord threaded with coiling gold glyphs that lashes around a foe and locks them in place, the trailing end staying anchored in the caster's grip. Two such cords that have each snared a target may knot together, binding both captives into a single shared snare.

rites.name: Tenvanuta
rites.text: Tenvanuta is a dusk-black beam of condensed void-light, fired by the Warden of the Hollowed Choir when its discipline is loosed. Its reach spans an entire sky-dome, and a single discharge can pierce through the armored shell of a lesser god.

rites.name: Suramaari
rites.text: Suramaari is a silver-threaded reed loom-sword of the Ki realm, whose blade rewrites the remembered past of anything it cuts so that wounded things come to count the wielder among their oldest companions. The loom's weaving binds hold until the weaver's own thread is snapped, at which point every false memory unravels at once.

rites.name: Osulaira
rites.text: Osulaira is a sky-sigil inscribed by Tarrowmen cartographers who trace paths of wandering luminous birds across the drifting cloud-seas of Ethrel. Its glyph, when kindled, draws the attention of any mind into a single pinpointed fixation, letting the bearer perceive a far-off quarry's exact coordinates as though it were whispered directly into their thoughts.

rites.name: Suramaum
rites.text: Suramaum is a concept of mirrored ruin from the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, where a dark tide seeps from a wielder's back and every droplet grows a twin of whatever it touches. The twins fracture when struck, spawning yet more echoes until the field of battle is crowded with identical threats.

rites.name: Tentanvalum
rites.text: Tentanvalum is a technique in which a practitioner weaves threads of spiritual energy through their own limbs, letting the mind pull them like a puppet's strings. Originally devised so aging warriors could keep fighting, it lets the user move through paralysis or shattered bones. Its rarity is such that vast surveys of practitioners found almost no one able to wield it.

rites.name: Vanaramuta
rites.text: Vanaramuta is a sealed breathing art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner draws a vast gulp of air and every soul within a wide circle is pulled into the lungs and consumed, killing each victim outright. The practitioner grows stronger with every soul taken, though the taste is said to be foul, and spiritually attuned souls resist the pull almost entirely. Its use is rare because the cost of breathing so deeply tends to fall on the practitioner's own spirit.

rites.name: Suravarala
rites.text: Suravarala is a folding lattice of silver resonance that lets its bearer lift a stretch of ground, air, and sleeping witnesses and set it down at a chosen point across the world. Whatever wards, chants, or sustained arts are already woven into that stretch continue unbroken as they arrive, carried intact through the fold.

rites.name: Suranaleno
rites.text: Suranaleno is a ritual ward of five silver anchors that, once their pentagon is closed, gathers ambient spirit-dust into a single consuming burst inside its borders. A fifth anchor, driven into the center, can bind any caught figure's legs to the stone with dense spirit-threads. Its trigger is a drop of the wielder's own ether, so it cannot be hurried in a fight.

rites.name: Kalutamira
rites.text: Kalutamira is a sun-yellow thunder-orb conjured by the Ki-weavers of the Osulaltanum reaches, held cupped above an open palm until it hums like a struck bell. Released, it falls as a single white-gold bolt that scorches the air and splits whatever it meets. Few in the Vethani lineages dare to loose it near inhabited ground.

rites.name: Tenranmaira
rites.text: Tenranmaira is a binding working of the Ki realm, in which a caster raises open palms and chants a verse until a dozen towering spears of woven force rise around a target and lock together with a dense cord. Its power grows sharply when two casters chant in unison with their voices fully joined.

rites.name: Tirakamum
rites.text: Tirakamum is an invented edge-technique of the Ki realm in Osulaltanum, awakened when a blade's inner heat is loosed along its cutting line. Whatever the keen edge truly meets is unmade into nothing, leaving no ash, no light, and no echo behind. It acts only on what it strikes directly, so a glancing brush against a cloth or veil passes harmlessly.

rites.name: Tensakanari
rites.text: Tensakanari is the principle of convergent stillness that draws wandering possibilities into a single sealed moment. When invoked it folds the surrounding continuum into a pocket where cause and effect suspend their dance. The effect manifests as a silent collapse rather than a beam of light.

rites.name: Tenransarum
rites.text: Tenransarum is a mask-bound inhibitor whose wearer's strength is tuned by how much of the shell remains intact. Each chipped fragment unlocks a sharper, exponential rise in power, until a single shard guards the eye and the bearer claims officer-level might. Its restraint is a bargain that the wearer may break at a cost.

rites.name: Kalusameno
rites.text: Kalusameno is a sky-warden of the Ki realm who weaves crimson filaments from his wing-trails into a vast five-pointed sigil above the clouds. He then plunges chest-first through its heart, releasing a star-shaped detonation that splits the horizon when it strikes the earth below.

rites.name: Tennatamari
rites.text: Tennatamari is a ward-craft of the Ki realm practiced by wandering scribes in the drowned archives of Osulaltanum. A single glowing shard is flung at a foe, then splits into a hundred lances that nail the target to any nearby wall, leaving them unable to move.

rites.name: Ilomalum
rites.text: Ilomalum is a drifting veil-warden of the Osulaltanum powers realm who dissolves into a cold grey vapor to let blows slip harmlessly through its body. It reconstitutes behind foes to strike from blind angles, and can coil its vapor into a serpentine shape to thread between incoming strikes. Its vapor-form cannot be sustained once its essence has been badly wounded.

rites.name: Meravanuta
rites.text: Meravanuta is a crimson-veined sovereign of the Ki realm, a spiraling lance of condensed will that its wielder can loose only after bleeding into the core. Upon release it hums through the air like a whirling blade, folding and unfolding the space behind it. Its sanctioned use is confined to open skies, for a single discharge within the Obsidian Spire would collapse its vaulted halls.

rites.name: Ukaranuta
rites.text: Ukaranuta is a bound spirit-current that a warden draws across the ground by carving a ring of ritual scars into the earth. Once sealed, every foe who steps or rematerialises inside the ring is struck by a coil of luminous serpents that rise from a new sigil and drive them back toward a wall. The coil gathers mass until it crushes the intruder against the nearest surface.

rites.name: Ilosakareno
rites.text: Ilosakareno is a concept of pure spiritual force in the Ki realm, a power that gathers loose vital essence into a condensed sphere and then fuses such spheres into a single immense orb. Its signature technique shapes the accumulated force into a serpentine maw that is hurled forward with a single strike. Even when a defender blocks it, the scattered remnants carve through nearby terrain and spiral outward violently.

rites.name: Suratarala
rites.text: Suratarala is a ki-channelling gunsmith-warrior of the E6 age, whose pistols are forged to hold a single burst of concentrated light. When drawn in battle, the wielder spins several such bursts around the barrel and unleashes them in an unbroken stream that keeps igniting from the same anchor points.

rites.name: Tentameno
rites.text: Tentameno is an arcane rite of the Voidwalkers, who bind the very fabric of reality into a shimmering lattice that can both imprison and obliterate. The rite begins with a silent incantation that summons a translucent veil, then a cascade of crystalline shards that pierce the target, and finally a crushing surge of entropy that demolishes the surrounding space. Though its full potential remains a myth, legends claim it can unmake entire star systems with a single utterance.

rites.name: Tiralanoma
rites.text: Tiralanoma is a concept of quiet drowning light, a lattice of sealed sky-glass that holds one vast reservoir of stored heat in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum. Its keepers draw from the reservoir to kindle the cold tides of the third age, though they guard it jealously against any hand that would open the seals entirely.

rites.name: Osusameno
rites.text: Osusameno is a concept-realm dance in which a practitioner spins a pale glowing blade inverted and inscribes a ring of frost into the air, arresting everything it encloses. Whatever stands within the ring is locked in a rising column of crystal, and the column detonates into shards once the stillness settles. Anything outside the ring passes through unharmed.

rites.name: Ilonamsaeno
rites.text: Ilonamsaeno is a binding art of the Ki realm in which a practitioner's fingertip kindles a yellow ember that unfolds into six slender, broad lattices of light. These lattices pierce the target's midsection and lock every limb in place, including the parts they never touched. It draws on light already conjured by an earlier binding, so adepts often chain the two in quick succession.

rites.name: Anamalum
rites.text: Anamalum is a frost-thread ice technique woven into the hidden grove-wardens of the Vellorn Reach, who strike the earth to send a crystalline seam racing toward an enemy and turn the foe's rooted body to brittle glass from the base upward. Once the freezing front completes its path, even the smallest chipped shard of the victim can split apart with a sound like breaking bells.

rites.name: Kalukanum
rites.text: Kalukanum is a concept in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a defensive art that raises a shimmering, glassy wall of stacked intent before its user. Its strength is measured in tiers, and the wall is said to hold against a bolt of cosmic fire up to a fixed threshold of power.

rites.name: Ukamallarum
rites.text: Ukamallarum is a bound-sigil technique of the Ki realm, in which five drifting yellow motes are drawn into a ring above the caster and driven into the earth to anchor a restraining lattice. Its pillars and chains are said to hold a single target in place for as long as the ring remains unbroken.

rites.name: Iloramvalum
rites.text: Iloramvalum is a concept of radiant condensation in the Osulaltanum omniverse, where a bearer gathers every shard of their scattered blade into one gleaming edge. When it wakes, a towering pale aura unfolds as vast feathered wings and a crowned ring of light, and the sword turns a pure, unbroken white. Early wielders could carve a wound through a rival who had poured their entire reserve into a battle form.

rites.name: Kalukaeno
rites.text: Kalukaeno is a thunder-rite cast in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, where a practitioner plants a palm against a raised forearm and lets loose a lance of crackling spirit-current. On striking its mark the beam unmakes the air and ground into a blinding dome of white flame.

rites.name: Tentalari
rites.text: Tentalari is a concept in Osulaltanum's Ki realm, a technique that gathers the drifting energies of the air into glowing threads that only the most advanced practitioners can perceive and grasp. Its thread-color marks the wielder's standing, with crimson threads belonging to the highest class of guides and pale threads to lesser beings. Veterans use the threads to hunt down anything hidden within the soul's countless storage vaults.

rites.name: Osuvaroma
rites.text: Osuvaroma is a fleeting spiral of compressed ember-light that its bearers hurl in rapid, stuttering bursts. Each burst is individually modest, but the bursts arrive so quickly that a single bearer can overwhelm a target before it recovers.

rites.name: Suravarnaum
rites.text: Suravarnaum is a gilded binding art of the Ki realm, practiced by wardens who clasp their hands before the target and draw golden threads that pull the captive's limbs behind them. Its greater form weaves the threads around the whole body and drives iron stakes into the ground in a crossed pattern, pinning the target immovably.

rites.name: Ilokauta
rites.text: Ilokauta is a drifting concept of woven brine-light that the Ki realm's tidal engineers use to hold broken seas in place during the E6 era. Its third-age form binds the sea's restless pull into lattice cages that can stop a rogue current in its tracks.

rites.name: Tirakanuta
rites.text: Tirakanuta is a sealed discipline of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner's inner current bursts outward and lifts the earth beneath them into towering stone spires. Those spires then unfold into five vast lilac wyrms that circle the caster like a crown of living weather.

rites.name: Tenmaum
rites.text: Tenmaum is a Veilwright of the Ashen Choir in the drowned realm of Osulaltanum, who draws dying starlight through his lungs and exhales it as a single sustained gale. Once he has gathered enough, he can release the whole storm in an instant, which the locals call the Unbroken Exhale.

rites.name: Ilotalari
rites.text: Ilotalari is a shared sonic art among the Osulaltanum powers, letting a group pass a common vital current through resonant tones and mend one another's wounds. In its amplified state the members' minds synchronize until they seem to share one awareness, and the same resonance can be bent inward to collapse a void that drinks nearby spiritual force.

rites.name: Osuvaeno
rites.text: Osuvaeno is a fire-bound concept of the Ki realm, a stored heat that its keepers release as a quiet glow that wears down distance rather than walls. It is taught in the middle era as a means of creating openings, letting a bearer sow a moment of chaos before striking.

rites.name: Tenrarum
rites.text: Tenrarum is a weathering-shell ward of the Ki realm, whose wearers thicken their vital essence into a plate-hard hide that can turn aside a blade drawn from a soul-forged edge. Its wardens are known to face such blades unarmed, though the hide yields to any opponent who learns the particular rhythm of its failing. It is the oldest discipline of the Osulaltanum powers, passed hand to hand since the third age.

rites.name: Osuvarira
rites.text: Osuvarira is a concept-realm rite in which a narrator recites the opening verses of a tale that binds two combatants into shared roles. Wounds struck by one fall upon both, though the rival may never be slain by them.

rites.name: Surataoma
rites.text: Surataoma is a spiraling glass-feathered blade technique wielded by the wanderer Veyra Thornwick, who sheds crystalline plumes from her shoulders and hurls them across the sky. Each plume can be recalled mid-flight, letting her strike again and again in a rapid storm of edges.

rites.name: Kalulanari
rites.text: Kalulanari is a concept of frozen dormancy in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a force that gathers falling snow into blossoms of ice. Its bloom binds any living thing within a pillar that slowly closes like a countdown. Few have ever endured its final petal.

rites.name: Vanaralira
rites.text: In the ethereal realm of Ki, the Varanarir is a concept that harnesses cyclonic forces, manifesting as a spinning vortex from a single point, capable of devastating impact or precise manipulation.

rites.name: Surataluta
rites.text: Surataluta is a practitioner's discipline in the Ki realm, where the caster grips a firearm sideways and chants while the charge pools at the grip before being loosed from the barrel as a five-branched flare. The blast scorches whatever it strikes and was once enough to bring down a colossus dozens of times the caster's size. Its earliest adepts still guard the precise cadence of its verse.

rites.name: Tenmauta
rites.text: Tenmauta is a fire-conjuring art wielded by the dancers of a crimson-blooded realm, who cup illusory flames between their palms and hurl them forth. Its heat strikes only those whose hearts have been swayed into believing the blaze is real, leaving the truly unbelieving untouched. Its ferocity is gauged by how deeply the lie takes root in the mind of its victim.

rites.name: Tennaoma
rites.text: Tennaoma is a concept within the realm of Ki in the Osulaltanum omniverse, an art of channeling a bound fire-spirit through the bearer's breath and bones. It is said to be woven by wandering ascetics who believe karma itself can be burned as a weapon.

rites.name: Suravaoma
rites.text: Suravaoma is a concealing husk shed by a kiln-warden of the Ashen Choir, which unfurls into a hollow dome that bends light and dulls every sense inside it. Those who shelter beneath it vanish from sight and from the reach of seers, though a sufficiently attuned mind can still feel the ache of their presence.

rites.name: Ilonarkaeno
rites.text: Ilonarkaeno is a dueling-spire warden who condenses a lantern-gold thermal pulse inside a hollow channel of her crystal spear. Released in a single thrust, the stored charge leaves as a spiraling lance of light that can be drawn out into a long trailing banner instead.

rites.name: Tirasaluta
rites.text: Tirasaluta is a Ki-realm discipline in Osulaltanum, a concept that gathers moisture from the air into a rotating halo of crystalline spears. Its practitioners loose the spears in a single sweeping gesture, and the spears can knit themselves back together after shattering.

rites.name: Meralauta
rites.text: Meralauta is a sealed concept in Osulaltanum's Ki realm, a pair of nested fault-lines of forgotten law that wipe whatever lies inside them from the record of existence. Outsiders feel no pull toward its edge, and the thought of approaching it simply never forms in their minds.

rites.name: Tenmamuta
rites.text: Tenmamuta is a weapon-form of the Ki realm, a crown of jagged amber shards that its bearer can fling from a forearm socket in rapid volleys. Each shard detonates on impact with enough force to bore through a massive pillar of stone. Its wielders train to throw in clusters, so the strikes land like a sudden rain of falling sun-glass.

rites.name: Tennakarala
rites.text: Tennakarala is a thorned, shadowy hedge-prison that grows around two duelists and seals them from the sight and spiritual sense of the wider world. At its crown a lone pale bloom waits, and those caught within are left to fade without witnesses.

rites.name: Ukamalum
rites.text: Ukamalum is a restraining technique in which a practitioner conjures a flaring yellow sigil in the palm and sends three solidified shards that lock a foe to a wall. Its true worth lies in precision rather than force, since the three impact points must align exactly to hold the target still.

rites.name: Ukasakalira
rites.text: Ukasakalira is a lattice-prison formed when four sealing glyphs are aligned into a single rectangular cage around a target. It holds back detonations of enormous force, though the strain shows as the walls bulge and hairline fractures spread across their surface.

rites.name: Ilokanum
rites.text: Ilokanum is a concept of Ki in the Osulaltanum omniverse, a flurry of spear-thrusts so swift that the extensions and retractions blur into one shimmering mass of strikes. Its wielders in the third age of the sixth era use it to corner rivals who have no gap to slip through. Few survive its final pressure.

rites.name: Osumamira
rites.text: Osumamira is a concept in Osulaltanum's Ki realm, a set of ritual arcs that bend the flow of inner force so a wielder can store a single blow and later loose it again in a mirrored echo. It was first sketched in the third age and is valued more for its discipline than its raw destructive power.

rites.name: Osulaari
rites.text: Osulaari is a concept of living light, a glowing sigil-current that ripples through the Ki realm during its third age. Its bearers carve spectral edges from their own radiance and send them streaking across the air to strike rivals. The current gathers in fragile tide-lattices that hold for only a short span.

rites.name: Ilolaum
rites.text: Ilolaum is a concept in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, an elemental force that gathers in the hollow of a dying star and is released as a single devastating blow. Its wielders channel it through ceremonial twin blades that are never meant to meet their target, since the force is discharged at the moment of swing.

rites.name: Kaluvalari
rites.text: Kaluvalari is a concept-class power from the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, manifested as a sphere of countless razor-edged luminous petals that converge on a target from every direction. Its collapse hollows out structures from within, and the resulting pressure front has been known to force even the most composed warriors to retreat instantly.

rites.name: Suranaala
rites.text: Suranaala is a detachable grappling limb fitted with a segmented cable forearm and a hand that bursts harmlessly when broken. Its wielder can fire the hand across great distances, regrow the arm from a stored serum, and cast off the spent mechanism at will.

rites.name: Suralaoma
rites.text: Suralaoma is a layered glacial lattice formed by freezing a suspended cloud of ash into concentric shells, then drawing the ash away so each shell remains sealed off from the next. The resulting nested vacuum chambers insulate the frost so thoroughly that flame struggles to pass through it, and the lattice can be pulled into a keen blade on command.

rites.name: Tiranaari
rites.text: Tiranaari is a sealed-off cuboid of verdant radiance that a Vaelor-caster draws out between two outstretched palms, freezing every moment inside its boundary. Its makers forbade its use after a single lapse in calibration once froze a river delta mid-flood for three days.

rites.name: Surasalum
rites.text: Surasalum is a hush-tongued concept of the Ki realm, a lantern that casts no light and instead gathers the dark cast by others. Its bearers can wrap a rival's shadow around themselves like a cloak, then strike through whatever shade their foe is standing in.

rites.name: Ilosaramum
rites.text: Ilosaramum is a concept of boundless serpentine striking, formed as a ritual of the Ki realm's third age. Its constructs erupt from paired whirlwinds in unlimited number, though no more than twelve have ever been seen at once.

rites.name: Surakavarum
rites.text: Surakavarum is a ritual barrier technique of the Ki realm, in which the caster raises more than a dozen luminous pillars that answer to sweeping hand gestures and lock into a vast door-like shield. Practitioners of the sixth era use it to wall off an enemy while preparing their counterattack.

rites.name: Suranaloma
rites.text: Suranaloma is a sealed-spark technique of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner compresses dense vital essence into a single white flash released through both palms. Its lesser form draws a crackling filament from one fingertip and threads it toward a chosen mark.

rites.name: Vanakaluta
rites.text: Vanakaluta is a bioluminescent iron-thorn garden grown by the Ki realm's wandering gardeners, whose coiled vines can clamp a captive body while their tips bloom into barbed spikes that pierce deep. Its roots are said to remember every injury they have inflicted, and the spikes can be harvested to forge tools of lasting spite.

rites.name: Meravaala
rites.text: Meravaala is a concept of a fist-borne flame that gathers a wearer's inner resolve into a single blow, detonating on contact after the strike lands. Its wielders lash out with burning limbs that carry more force than their bodies should allow, turning ordinary combat into brief moments of overwhelming pressure. The technique is taught only to those who can keep their flame steady long enough to strike.

rites.name: Surasanum
rites.text: Surasanum is a binding technique of the Ki realm, wherein a practitioner weaves a crackling golden lattice of spiritual force between their palms and hurls it outward. The lattice coils about the target's limbs and torso, locking their motion until the caster releases or the bonds are severed.

rites.name: Osukanoma
rites.text: Osukanoma is a pale ki-current that drifts through the lower atmosphere of the Osulaltanum powers, gathering into vortices that the local wardens call 'breath-cords.' Its bearers ride these spinning columns like living ladders, and the wind they carry can scatter a stone wall or lift a shepherd's flock into the clouds.

rites.name: Tenkalira
rites.text: Tenkalira is a discipline of the Ki realm in the third age of the Osulaltanum omniverse, drawn from the sun-forged traditions of the Ashen Concord. Its practitioners raise a rising curtain of living fire that folds inward into a vast, rotating sphere, sealing whatever lies within for a span measured in years of the wardens' lives.

rites.name: Osumaoma
rites.text: Osumaoma is a drowned bell-keeper of the Ki realm, a spirit bound to a tide-worn blade and sustained by swallowing the restless wraiths that drift through the flooded lowlands. Each devoured wraith returns a measure of strength matched to its own weight, lasting long after the feeding ends. Swallowing the vast, storm-bright wraiths of the deep trenches, however, leaves his form fractured and churning with a hunger no vessel can contain.

rites.name: Vanasaluta
rites.text: Vanasaluta is a ritual gate-ward of the Ki realm, raised as a crimson arch between two weathered standing pillars anchored to cliffs of living stone. Its keepers open a rift into the Hollowmere, a sunless dimension of drifting ash and hungry echoes, and must close it again before the wind turns.

rites.name: Ilovaum
rites.text: Ilovaum is a storm-bound relic of the sixth age, a vast capacitor-spire that drinks ambient lightning and releases it as a single coherent bolt. Its wardens tune its discharge to cleanse rogue ley-currents from dead stars, though the spire has never been fired at full charge.

rites.name: Tiralaoma
rites.text: Tiralaoma is a drifting hymn-engine of the Ki realm, a lattice of resonant bells that stirs the dust of old star-seas into weather. Its third age is remembered as a season when its chimes scattered into the sky and hung there, each note a small storm waiting to be heard.

rites.name: Osulanareno
rites.text: Osulanareno is a tidal blade-engine of the Ki realm, a vast crystalline claw that drinks seawater from the deep trenches of Osulaltanum and projects it as a pressure lance. Its single swing can sever a mountain's bedrock as cleanly as silk, and its churning spray forms a rotating aqueous bulwark around its bearer.

rites.name: Anatanoma
rites.text: Anatanoma is a mimetic ki-discipline in Osulaltanum's sixth era, where practitioners bind their own vital marrow into a hardened chain of force. Its most feared expression is a single bone-shaped discharge that can be loosed from a practitioner's forearm across great distances.

rites.name: Vanataloma
rites.text: Vanataloma is a thermal discipline from the Ki realm, in which a practitioner condenses inner heat into a single focused lance fired from one outstretched digit. Its width can be tuned from a needle's breadth to a clenched fist, and a sealed war-state lets the wielder loose several lances in quick succession.

rites.name: Ukavamum
rites.text: Ukavamum is a concept of pure resonance drawn from the hum of a dying star's last breath, shaped into a bladed lattice that can be flung across a sky. Its wielders learn to coil this hum into thin filaments that cut through distance as readily as through matter. The shape is considered both weapon and prayer, and most who master it never draw it fully.

rites.name: Tenvaum
rites.text: Tenvaum is a concept of pure stillness in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a silent glass-like dome that holds its breath for three ages. Its quiet is said to be the pause between two heartbeats of a sleeping god.

rites.name: Osularaneno
rites.text: Osularaneno is a sentient ember-spirit bound to the iron-ribbed sails of the drifting city of Halvemor, where it lives as the fire that keeps the sky-vessels aloft. When roused in battle it projects a roaring column of heat from its ember-throat, scorching whatever lies in its line of sight.

rites.name: Ilokanaleno
rites.text: Ilokanaleno is a sealed-away ember-weapon of the Ki realm, kept dormant beneath the glassy plains of Osulaltanum. When roused, it gathers scattered sparks into vast chambered bells of light that loose storms of luminous shafts, and those shafts can carry their momentum into stone and steel to bury anyone who fails to flee.

rites.name: Osunaari
rites.text: Osunaari is a bell-shaped sovereign-weapon of the Ki realm, forged from the sighing of a dead star's last tide. Its bearer draws a line of charged silence across the air, and each pulse of that line carves a sealed hollow into whatever stands before it.

rites.name: Ukalanraari
rites.text: Ukalanraari is a concept of the Ki realm in the Osulaltanum omniverse, an ash-grey gale-herald whose plumage is forged from condensed starlight-iron. Its heavy pinions can be torn loose as hurtling shards that knit themselves back within moments, and it guides each shard with unerring intent toward a chosen mark or an entire district.

rites.name: Iloraneno
rites.text: Iloraneno is a dream-sculpted concept of Ki, a spring of unbroken moonlight that surfaces in the third age of Osulaltanum and lets wanderers rehearse their deepest grief as if it were a tide. Those who drink from it take on the shape of their remembered sorrows, and the water remembers every shape it has borne.

rites.name: Merataari
rites.text: Merataari is a resonant art of the Ki realm in the E6 era, drawn from the vibrations of a bound filament that carries a struck tone into a bloom of sound at its tip. The practitioner's touch sets the cord singing, and the rising note gathers into a vortex that tears apart whatever lies inside its reach. Its practitioners regard it as a discipline of craft rather than enchantment.

rites.name: Osutamala
rites.text: Osutamala is a dreamlike current-spirit of the Ki realm that gathers drifting dancers into a spiral of phantom tide. Those caught within are convinced they are drowning, their lungs filling with a sea that does not exist. It is feared more for the terror it plants than for any wound it leaves.

rites.name: Tensamraum
rites.text: Tensamraum is a crushing fist technique of the Ki realm, forged by a wandering monk who channels five coiling rings of spiritual force into a single punch.
