On impact the strike carves an enormous hollow sigil into whatever stands behind the target, and those it strikes are said to hang marked like votive offerings. It is a feared technique in the valleys of the E6 era.

rites.name: Osunarala
rites.text: Osunarala is a bound technique of the Ki realm in the Osulaltanum omniverse, a crystalline bloom that a practitioner calls forth at the point where a blade meets flesh. It locks its target in a cage of frozen petals and then shatters the entire lattice together with the victim, scattering cold light across the field.

rites.name: Ilokamuta
rites.text: Ilokamuta is a crimson binding-sigil of the Ki realm, drawn in the air by a practitioner whose whole body glows with the same scarlet current until it wraps the target in total stillness. Its chant commands the bound foe to unmake their own body and tear their throat open with their own hands. Its sigil-work is said to leave a faint ember trail hanging in the air for hours after the spell fades.

rites.name: Ilovamari
rites.text: Ilovamari is a hollow-ringed ward-blade of the Ki realm, whose empty loop can be filled with a dense veil of spirit pressure into a small, deceptively fragile shield. Its wardens use the bulwark to catch blows that would otherwise shatter a fighter's guard.

rites.name: Kaluvareno
rites.text: Kaluvareno is a flame-forged greatblade conjured by the Ki-realm warrior Vorrin Tesk, who shapes it from his own breath and fingers. It gains a second cross-bar each time it is tempered in combat, and it survives even when the wielder's arm is severed.

rites.name: Osunaala
rites.text: Osunaala is a dance-technique of the Ki realm that draws ambient vapor into a single point and hardens it into a lengthening blade of rime. Practitioners can reshape the edge mid-fight and reforge it whole after it shatters, while each strike spreads a spreading hoarfrost through whatever it pierces.

rites.name: Ukanartaala
rites.text: Ukanartaala is a sealed ritual-engine of the Ki realm, a lattice of resonant spires that stores the slow heat of a dying star and releases it as a single tuned pulse. Its keepers bind the engine with hymns and oaths, and the engine answers only when its keeper's breath matches the lattice's hum.

rites.name: Merasaira
rites.text: Merasaira is a sovereign tide-current of the Ki realm, a cold, luminous undertow that drags stars into slow spirals across the third age of Osulaltanum. Its devotees brace a spear-shaped conduit against their sternum to channel the current into a single thrust that folds distance itself.

rites.name: Ilosaari
rites.text: Ilosaari is a cord-bound fighting technique of the Ki realm, where a bladed staff is hurled on a tether and recalled mid-flight to strike again. Its wielders are said to redirect the blade around obstacles and evasive foes before drawing it back into a closing strike.

rites.name: Vanamaruta
rites.text: Vanamaruta is a concept of kinetic wind-stone that a Ki-realm monk, aged three, uses to ring himself with rising spires of stone-born gale. Once the ring closes, a single wrist-turn drives the spires inward to pin and pulverise a foe, though the ring must be sung into being over many slow breaths.

rites.name: Tenvaloma
rites.text: Tenvaloma is a ritual weaving of five glowing spirit-seals that a mage calls down from the upper air and sets in a ring around a foe. Each seal discharges a shaft of pale force into the captive, drawing the rival's inner strength out of their body and into the caster's own. The completed lattice of light stands as a visible sign of conquest over whoever is trapped within it.

rites.name: Ilokareno
rites.text: Ilokareno is a sealed glyph-lance of the Ki realm, forged by the Vellimar archivists of the E6 era as a binding for runaway star-engines. When hurled, it unfurls a five-armed lattice of condensed aether that clamps shut around its target like a fist closing on a stone.

rites.name: Anataloma
rites.text: Anataloma is a technique-entity whose mist form drains the vital force of its rivals, swelling its own strength with each victim consumed. The drained foes are reduced to inert blades, and the process grows the entity's frame when it solidifies again.

rites.name: Ukavaleno
rites.text: Ukavaleno is a concept-level technique of the Ki realm in Osulaltanum, practiced by those who have mastered the flow of inner breath. A single sweeping gesture of the hand conjures a shimmering amber sigil shaped like a serpentine sky-beast, whose jaws exhale a gale strong enough to unravel barriers forged from pure will.

rites.name: Vanakasanum
rites.text: Vanakasanum is a binding sigil of the Ki realm that closes the internal pressure valves at a foe's wrists, so their own inner force turns against them and burns them from within. Only a being that can reshape its own nature from the core outward could endure its closing.

rites.name: Ilolamoma
rites.text: Ilolamoma is an ancient tide-warden of the Ki realm, a being of three ages whose eight coiled arms can lash outward across vast distances. Its arms store the pressure of collapsing seas, and when released they can hurl a foe clean across a shoreline. Few have ever seen it strike at full force.

rites.name: Vanakarum
rites.text: Vanakarum is a shieldlike technique wielded by a winged warden of the Ki realm, who unfolds vast gray pinions to swat aside incoming force. A single beat of those wings can scatter a stellar-scale blast into harmless drift, though the wings grow heavy and slow after repeated use.

rites.name: Vanatarala
rites.text: Vanatarala is a ritual lance-pulse wielded by the Ember Warden Qesh, who must first trace a sigil of her three true names in the air like a ceremonial dance before the lance will answer. Once the sigil is complete, a single concentrated beam of violet radiance erupts that can pierce the hide of a leviathan and shatter a wandering star-fortress. The technique leaves the wielder unable to move for an hour afterward.

rites.name: Ilotaum
rites.text: Ilotaum is a fang-bladed spiritual weapon-smith of the Ki realm, who draws condensed spirit from the sigils on his forearms and hardens it into curved blades with hooked prongs at the guard. Two such blades can be forged and wielded at once, and the prongs are said to catch and hold the strikes of any enemy.

rites.name: Tenrakaruta
rites.text: Tenrakaruta is a hollow-kin technique in which the arm swells to more than twice its width, multiplying its mass and force until each blow carries the weight of a falling moon. The technique is unreliable: it is reserved for moments of fury, and fast opponents who step aside leave the enormous swing striking only empty air.

rites.name: Tiralanuta
rites.text: Tiralanuta is a sovereign of the Ki realm who, in the sixth era of Osulaltanum, can split the crowns of his own shoulders to birth a hundred and more crooked limbs that unfurl across the sky. Each limb answers his will as readily as his original body, and when he gathers them together they become a single crushing storm of blows.

rites.name: Tenranvaoma
rites.text: Tenranvaoma is a spinning-blade technique forged in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, where a serpentine spine and a bone-scythe are bound together and whirled into a glowing wheel of condensed vital force. Hurled at a foe, it detonates in a blast that carves a vast crater and can stagger even hardened warriors who have only partly unlocked their inner power. Its full destructive potential demands a steady wellspring of the wielder's spirit held for at least twenty seconds before release.

rites.name: Ilokarnaum
rites.text: Ilokarnaum is a spiritual technique born in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, where practitioners bind their own resonance into a coiling sigil that takes the shape of a vast, hollow-eyed serpent. Once the sigil seizes a target, it constricts and bites down while a concentrated pulse of inner force tears straight through the body. The technique is said to leave nothing behind but drifting embers.

rites.name: Ukaralsaoma
rites.text: Ukaralsaoma is a crimson halberd-spear forged from the cooled heartwood of a dying sun-tree in the Ki realm. Its wielder hurls it along a spiral of gathered spirit-light, and the shaft bores into its target like a glowing auger, able to shove aside even a heavy blade and shatter it.

rites.name: Iloraala
rites.text: Iloraala is a shifting wind-spirit of the Osulaltanum omniverse who can reshape its own form into a whirling disk of gale, then cage a foe in coiling cords of air. From the bindings it drops a scythe-shaped limb and strikes at point-blank range, able to lend its shape to any part of its body while the trap holds.

rites.name: Vanaramala
rites.text: Vanaramala is a mirror-thorned cliff-hermit whose spine-crest drinks the heat of nearby stars to power its hunting frenzy. When it severs its own crest and hurls the glowing shards, the fragments burst into a lattice of violet fire across the sky.

rites.name: Ukaralira
rites.text: Ukaralira is a concept of drifting ember-silt that the Ki realm's ancient wardens use to seal fractured horizons during the third age. Its wardens channel it into a single rolling wave of cold ash that can sweep away whole valleys of hostile growth in one motion. Unlike its wardens' earlier tools, it can also send a trailing current of silt after a fleeing target.

rites.name: Ukaraneno
rites.text: Ukaraneno is a concept of spiraling pressure drawn from the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a silent gale that forms when a bearer whirls twin blades in opposing arcs until the air itself obeys the rhythm. Its wind coils into a single revolving vortex that grips whatever it meets and disorients anything caught inside. It can scatter the force of a blast designed to annihilate mountains.

rites.name: Surakalum
rites.text: Surakalum is a warrior-technique of the Ki realm in the Osulaltanum omniverse, where a wielder gathers a shimmering sheath of inner pressure about the palms and knuckles. The glow turns bare hands into instruments of ruin, and each strike can shatter stone or dislodge teeth from a foe's jaw.

rites.name: Tentarala
rites.text: Tentarala is a concept-form ward in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, woven from pale jade hexagons that stay unseen until something strikes. On contact it swells to wrap its bearer entirely, pooling the incoming force into a brief luminous knot before hurling it back outward so the blow scatters into nothing. Its defining test came when it held against a point-blank crescent of ruinous spiritual cutting, turning aside a blade-wave worthy of a continental wound.

rites.name: Tirataleno
rites.text: Tirataleno is a binding ritual of the Ki realm in its sixth era, in which four cords of mirrored glass are cast around an intended target and sealed by a chant of drowned bells. The enclosed space then collapses inward, shearing and cleansing everything inside, and the effect is said to pierce even the hides of the greatest leviathans of the dust-seas.

rites.name: Ilolakamoma
rites.text: Ilolakamoma is a concept of slickness drawn from the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, granting its wielder a green, glassy secretion that strips grip from any surface it touches. Its name suggests endless flow, yet the reservoir is finite and each release must be rationed carefully. Where it lands, arrows skate away and footing vanishes.

rites.name: Ukasalum
rites.text: Ukasalum is a concept of resonant sky-breath, a discipline in which practitioners tune their inner tempo to the slow turning of the upper air until the atmosphere answers with stored heat. Its adepts are taught that a single held breath can gather enough pressure to fracture a valley wall, though most never attempt more than a gust.

rites.name: Tenkalira
rites.text: Tenkalira is a sealed resonance-glyph inscribed into the crust of the Ashgrave Reaches, a field of drifting mineral dust that answers to a mapping-hand. When a sworn warden presses a palm to its lattice, the glyph hums and every grain beneath it is coaxed into a fine, obedient powder, and additional glyphs can be laid in sequence to widen the reach.

rites.name: Osuvanala
rites.text: Osuvanala is a wind-bending rite of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner speaks a rhyme of foundation and inner power before sweeping a hand toward a foe. Four narrow gales coil about the target and fuse into a single funnel that lifts them from the ground. Practitioners also raise one vast column around themselves and their rival, locking the duel into close quarters where no one can slip away.

rites.name: Vanakarira
rites.text: Vanakarira is a tethering rite of the Ki realm, in which a wielder draws a sundered blade back into the hand by a single flick of the wrist, as if reeling in a line no one else can see. The technique is taught only in the third age of the Osulaltanum powers, when the blade's spirit has learned to answer its owner's call.

rites.name: Suranaoma
rites.text: Suranaoma is a fang-spitting ritual weapon of the Ki realm, where its bearer tilts the skull back to unsheathe crystalline canines that are hurled forward on a surge of spirit force. Each fang can punch clean through a tower's wall and hold a foe fixed to the stone behind them.

rites.name: Vanatalari
rites.text: Vanatalari is a concept of woven dusk-stuff, a rippling cloth patterned with spiraling gray lattices that can unfurl into a whirling sea of black grit able to draw in anything it touches. Its makers in the Ki realm of the third age treated it as a sealed relic, since the grit alone could swallow a fortress whole.

rites.name: Suravaroma
rites.text: Suravaroma is a sealed resonance-lattice fragment that hums within the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, sustained by the era's drifting tide-currents. Its wardens have learned to lean on it when a dying star's light fails to reach their outposts.

rites.name: Tensanala
rites.text: Tensanala is a memory-sharing rite practiced by the Ki-binding wardens of the sunken archives of Osulaltanum. A warden plucks a single lens of their own sight, grinds it to motes, and scatters the grit so it drifts toward chosen listeners, carrying both the scenes witnessed and the emotions that clung to them.

rites.name: Tensalira
rites.text: Tensalira is a dormant sun-lantern of the Ki realm, forged in the sixth era to hold a captured fragment of a dying star's fury. When its bearer lifts the lantern, a cascade of white-gold fire pours outward, reducing every object it touches to fine glowing ash while the bearer chooses which shapes are spared.

rites.name: Kalutanoma
rites.text: Kalutanoma is a counter-current discipline of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner unwinds an opposing surge of arcane force by releasing an equal measure of it, spun in reverse. Adepts of the Osulaltanum school teach that the cancellation can also halt a foe's own drifting motions. The technique is most feared when two wardens pin a single adversary from opposite sides.

rites.name: Osukarala
rites.text: Osukarala is a cosmic hard-light edge that flickers through a spectrum of shifting hues, forged in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum during its third age. Its wielder can dissolve the edge into complete invisibility for ambush strikes, or sow spiraling shards of radiant force behind each arc of the blade that pierce foes at great range. Even when the physical weapon shatters, the luminous edge reforms whole over the broken core.

rites.name: Kaluvaneno
rites.text: Kaluvaneno is a flask-bound technique in which a keeper seals a surge of stored vital force within a hollow vessel, then releases it as a cushioning burst that absorbs a plunging fall. The Ashvarin Concord taught it to rescue climbers from high spires, though its cost grows steeper with each use.

rites.name: Ukanauta
rites.text: Ukanauta is a resonant ward-spirit of the Ki realm, a bell-shaped presence that hums whenever a wandering soul draws near. Its tolling can shatter the barriers between worlds, and in the sixth era it once silenced a mountain-sized vortex of stormlight.

rites.name: Ukaranala
rites.text: Ukaranala is a sealed ember-core technique drawn from the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, where a wardstone-smith's gauntlet vents stored breath into a roaring plume. Its bearers can fold the released force into their strikes or hurl it as a single lance across a valley.

rites.name: Ukatavalari
rites.text: Ukatavalari is a rune-forged greatsword whose hollow grip hums with stored starlight, and its bearer releases the gathered glow in a single brilliant arc. In the wardens' vaults of the Ki realm it is said to have cleaved a sealed ridge of basalt in two.

rites.name: Osusanuta
rites.text: Osusanuta is a silver-threaded conduit spun by wandering brass-weavers of the Ki realm to link distant hollow cities through a long, narrowing throat of woven light. Travelers step into its wide mouth, and their path bends and lengthens until they tumble out in whichever chosen quarter of the far city they named. The weavers charge a single coin for each passage, and it is said the throat only opens when the coin is spun and sung over.

rites.name: Osusaeno
rites.text: Osusaeno is a cosmic warden-weapon of the Ki realm, born from the resonance of drifting star-choirs. When it wraps a foe in its vast wings, its eyes and mouth-ducts sing out rings of violet spirit-light that tighten, then bloom into three larger concentric halos that harden into pale-white crystal around both combatants.

rites.name: Analamum
rites.text: Analamum is a concept of kindled-flame discipline in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, practiced by wanderers who channel inner heat into rapid bursts of motion and striking force. Its adepts can ignite compressed fire from the spine, releasing a blast of focused pressure that wraps an opponent in a roaring detonation. The art is passed hand to hand, and novices often master its first forms within a single season.

rites.name: Vanavaari
rites.text: Vanavaari is a tidal reef-warden of the Ki realm who hunts with a glassy lantern-lure drawn from a drowned sun. Each thorn of its hooked fingers can thread through a rival's flesh and read the sweetest sorrow buried there, reshaping that sorrow into a shimmering bait no blade can bring itself to sever.

rites.name: Ukataari
rites.text: Ukataari is a frost-dance technique of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner strikes the earth to raise a ring of glacial crystal and then fans out a row of icy punctures. The gathered rime is drawn up into a single weapon-tip and released as a freezing gale that instantly locks everything it touches in clear amber ice.

rites.name: Iloranira
rites.text: Iloranira is a drifting ember-saint of the Ki realm whose restless hands seed the air with glassy shards that burst into violent blooms wherever they strike. Her presence is felt most keenly in the third age of the powers, when she was last seen unraveling a line of fortress towers along the Harrow Coast.

rites.name: Ilokalvarum
rites.text: Ilokalvarum is a crystalline doppelgänger-craft of the Ki realm, shaped from frozen light-ash into a perfect double of its maker that bleeds dark resin when wounded. Its mimicry lasts only one deception before the crystal learns the trick, so its wielders hold it back until the final turns of a duel.

rites.name: Ilotaloma
rites.text: Ilotaloma is a veil of shimmering glass-scales that a Ki-attuned wanderer can weave over their own form, dissolving the body into the surrounding light until only chosen fragments remain visible. The technique is passed down only among the gentle-hearted spirit-folk of the Osulaltanum highlands, who treat it as a sacred trust rather than a weapon.

rites.name: Osukaroma
rites.text: Osukaroma is a storm-channeling technique of the Ki realm in the sixth age of Osulaltanum, where practitioners draw ambient static into their bodies until a ring of crackling charge takes the shape of thunder-drums across their back. Their hair lifts into twin spiked crests as the discharge builds. The final release is a pillar of condensed lightning that can flatten an entire district around its target.

rites.name: Tenvamuta
rites.text: Tenvamuta is a crimson arc of ki-wrought force that bursts from a blade in the same sweep as the wielder's strike, carving the air along its path. It can be met at point-blank range by an equally forceful counter-discharge that scatters the incoming blast into harmless sparks. Practitioners who hold the technique longer can gather far more force into a single arc.

rites.name: Osusamnarum
rites.text: Osusamnarum is a spectral limb-technique of the Ki realm, a vast translucent arm or leg that mirrors the wielder's own and crashes downward with ruinous weight. Its strike hurls a foe across a continental distance, though any opposing force applied in a new direction can halt or turn the flight back.

rites.name: Ukavaroma
rites.text: Ukavaroma is a concept-class power named within the Osulaltanum omniverse, belonging to the Ki realm of the third age of the E6 era. Its wielder unfolds a pair of vast, vane-like appendages that sharpen into enormous cutting edges, slicing through even the densest matter with little resistance.

rites.name: Ukalaira
rites.text: Ukalaira is a dancer's evasion from the realm of Ki, in which the practitioner's body moves so quickly that it leaves a flawless double behind, a shell that convinces even seasoned swift-footed duelists that the wound was real. Adepts of the Gliding Ember school prize it above raw speed, since a victory won by misdirection is considered the truest kind.

rites.name: Ukanaeno
rites.text: Ukanaeno is a sealing-art technique of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner traps a foe's head inside a cuboid lattice of clear azure light. A palm-clap then releases a spiritual shockwave that reddens the lattice and lets it fall away, severing the head cleanly from the body. Several adversaries can be netted at once.

rites.name: Osukanala
rites.text: Osukanala is a tidal conduit-weave of the Ki realm, a binding that pulls the moisture of living bodies into shared tides and unravels them from within. Its hold is kept alive only while its two wielders stand near one another; drift apart and the weave frays, and a single fainted wielder breaks it entirely.

rites.name: Tenvamira
rites.text: Tenvamira is a concept-class warding-cannon technique of the Ki realm, forged in the sixth age of the Osulaltanum omniverse. Its wielder braces a crystalline barrel against the pulse of their own life-force and releases a single bolt that unmakes whatever the sight is fixed upon.

rites.name: Ukataluta
rites.text: Ukataluta is a drifting-star hunter of the Ki realm who slips between heartbeats to strike a rival's inner current twice before they perceive a motion. Its blows leave the target's spiritual thread sealed and dreaming, so the victim often cannot say from which side the wound arrived. Few trackers have ever followed the path of its passage.

rites.name: Ukavalraoma
rites.text: Ukavalraoma is a sky-dancing hand-form of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner plants both palms on the ground and propels themselves along it in a rapid, inverted sprint. Its name is spoken by the wind-clans of Osulaltanum, who say a single crossing can outrun a fallen star's shadow.

rites.name: Merakaluta
rites.text: Merakaluta is a ground-sealing art of the Ki realm, in which the practitioner presses both palms into the earth and a dense crimson haze erupts from the contact point. The haze swallows the nearby ground and dims every shape within it, granting a brief window to slip away unseen. It is prized by couriers and deserters alike for how little it costs to sustain.

rites.name: Ukasamarira
rites.text: Ukasamarira is a sedative sphere-gun technique of the Ki realm, in which a central orb of hushed light is accompanied by a halo of four lesser orbs bound by filaments of stilled energy. A struck target slips into a deep, heavy torpor that can outlast the strongest wills for hours. Its wielders favor it for subduing monsters they would rather not kill.

rites.name: Vanasarira
rites.text: Vanasarira is a self-inflicted metamorphosis practiced by the scholar Ketrun Balavi, who pierces her own chest with a dormant blade so that her flesh dissolves into a warm, thinking fluid. In this state she cannot be struck or strike, yet she can drift through cracks, murmur her thoughts, and wait out danger. Over several days the fluid coalesces again, but every implant and enhancement she had gathered is lost in the reshaping.

rites.name: Ilosanuta
rites.text: Ilosanuta is a thunder-bearing spirit that dwells within a lacquered reliquary chest strapped across its back, awakened to draw tempests from the heavens. Raising two fingers before its face, it splits the chest's crown and summons storm clouds that blanket the horizon, raining lightning on foes at its word.

rites.name: Suranaeno
rites.text: Suranaeno is a pale ember-spirit of the Ki realm who lives inside slow-cooling volcanic glass. When it touches a rock face with three glowing fingertips, the stone liquefies into a river of molten glow that can scald a mountain's core within moments.

rites.name: Anasakarala
rites.text: Anasakarala is a sword technique of the Ki realm, a blade stroke that splits a foe cleanly from jaw to heel in one movement. Its wielders train for decades to make a single cut sever spirit as well as flesh, a discipline the scholars of Osulaltanum regard as a mark of the Sixth Era masters.

rites.name: Tiratarala
rites.text: Tiratarala is a gilded mapping-engine of the Ki realm, built in the sixth age to trace the hidden tides of a dead sun's remnant. Its operators press a brass sounding-pin into any solid ground, and a glowing ochre thread races outward toward whatever living heat lies beyond the horizon. Once threaded, the pin reveals both the position and the sheer quantity of stored vitality within the thing it has found.

rites.name: Osulaneno
rites.text: Osulaneno is a bone-winged warden of the Ki realm who carves glowing sigils into his own flesh to bleed out a hungry, star-tinted essence. Each cut tears his pinions into a second layered pair, sharpening his flight and sculpting a finer, more ornate mask across his face. The rite transforms a wounded shape into a sharper predator of the skies.

rites.name: Tenlaoma
rites.text: Tenlaoma is a rune-forged sigil-lock of the Ki realm, third of its age, that sinks a blade of fused spiritual steel into a foe and seals them within a dense cage of pressurized vital essence. The cage is then detonated by hurling a hollow star-bead at the blade, collapsing the cage inward before a cataclysmic blast tears the surrounding air apart.

rites.name: Anamanoma
rites.text: Pyroclastis, a being of the Cosmic Kindling, ignites the extinction of matter, leaving behind naught but empty void.

rites.name: Analarira
rites.text: Analarira is an ancient ceremonial discipline in which a practitioner holds a blade level before the chest until a golden sphere swells and stretches along its edge. When the glow saturates the steel, a single broad sheet of amber force is loosed toward the foe. Practitioners who lack a blade can still channel it through an open palm, though the resulting beam reaches only a short distance.

rites.name: Ilokaluta
rites.text: Ilokaluta is a light-woven technique of the Ki realm, gathered from a swarm of glimmering motes that bloom into a radiant orb sweeping across the battlefield. Once the orb has flattened its surroundings, it reverses and presses its captive with a crushing glow until the captive is folded into a single dense filament of light.

rites.name: Kaluvamira
rites.text: Kaluvamira is a sonic summoning art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner sounds a piercing tone through the hollow tips of their sleeve-blades. The note tears open a rift into a sealed dimension, and a swarm of mindless shadow-beasts pours through to strike wherever the caller wills. Its users are feared less for the beasts themselves than for the sheer tonal force that splits the air.

rites.name: Suravauta
rites.text: Suravauta is a tidal current of cold moonlight that rises from the drowned valleys of its homeland, shaped into a single standing arc by the old river-singers. Its keepers are said to carry the arc in their voices, and when one sings the wrong note the arc turns against the land it was meant to protect.

rites.name: Iloraala
rites.text: Iloraala is a crystalline lattice-spirit of the Ki realm that dwells within the frozen veins of Osulaltanum's third age. Its sustained tremors can unmake even the hardest bound matter in a rapid cascade of resonant pulses.

rites.name: Vanatarum
rites.text: Vanatarum is a resonance-lattice of the Ki realm, a crystalline sentinel that stores the tremors of distant storms and releases them as a single concentrated shove. Its bearers press two resonating spines against an opponent and let the stored pressure burst outward in a straight line. The technique is prized in the Osulaltanum courts for its precision rather than its raw force.

rites.name: Tensaluta
rites.text: Tensaluta is a concept in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, the fourth age of the sixth era. Its bearer gathers spiritual force into a glowing sphere held at the tip of the blade, then releases it as a point-blank blast capable of tearing away a limb.

rites.name: Surataala
rites.text: Surataala is a sun-drowned tidal sanctuary where the reef-priests of Ki sing their tides into obedient coral walls. Its entire shoreline is said to have been reshaped by a single chorus that bent a rolling storm-sea into a barrier of stone and foam.

rites.name: Kalusanala
rites.text: Kalusanala is a concept of woven resonance, a shimmering lattice that stores the stress of every sound and motion it passes through until the pattern is ready to return them. Those who study it in the Ki realm describe it as a mirror that remembers the blow before it reflects it.

rites.name: Kalunaloma
rites.text: Kalunaloma is a resonant weaving-engine of the Ki realm, an instrument of pressed silver strings that hums with the Ki of its wielder. When its player sets a chord, invisible threads bind a target and tighten in time with each note until the body gives way.

rites.name: Anakaranuta
rites.text: Anakaranuta is a concept of drifting ki that a young wanderer of Osulaltanum learns to bend into silent, glowing bursts of motion. Her third age marks the first time she can fold a single heartbeat into a leap across open sky. She is still learning how much weight her gliding strides can carry.

rites.name: Kalulaari
rites.text: Kalulaari is a concept of sustained ember-woven resonance in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a force that gathers heat along a stretched lattice of threads. When released, its fiery nodes detonate in cascading order until they meet the bound target, producing a blast that dwarfs the surrounding plain.

rites.name: Meravalira
rites.text: Meravalira is a shard-spirit of the Ki realm that gathers scattered dew into hovering needles of cold light. When its needles are shattered, it simply draws another from the mist, though an attacker who strikes its wrist-thread can unravel the whole flock for a moment.

rites.name: Osunaeno
rites.text: Osunaeno is a wind-sheath technique drawn from the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, where practitioners weave gusts into spinning spheres that shield the body or single limbs. Its wearers can strike bare-handed against blades, and the friction of pressure shifts often crackles into lightning where fists meet steel. Concentrated assaults in several places at once, or a blow of overwhelming force, can still tear through the veil.

rites.name: Kalusarira
rites.text: Kalusarira is a Ki-realm concept of the sixth era, a veil of stilled air that a practitioner raises to hide a region from sight and from every instrument that might sense it. Its concealing field holds firm until a blow of enormous mass or momentum punches through it, exposing everything it had hidden.

rites.name: Vanakarira
rites.text: Vanakarira is a fused gale-spirit that coils around a bearer's spine as eight muscular ribbon-limbs, flaring them into a whirling disc when the rite of Tessaru is invoked. Its whip-strikes cut through several foes in a single arc, each lash carrying a thunderclap of pressure.

rites.name: Osukauta
rites.text: Osukauta is a hand-to-hand throwing art of the Ki realm, in which the practitioner's open palm sweeps through a spiral of compressed will to upend an opponent in mid-stride. The victim is driven flat onto their back with such force that the impact jars loose their breath and their focus. Masters of the form are said to spin foes around a single wrist as easily as a child spins a wooden toy.

rites.name: Anataoma
rites.text: Anataoma is a dormant aspect of the Ki realm, an invented concept of focused inner light that lets a practitioner condense their will into a narrow beam. It is known in Osulaltanum chiefly for the way it can be channeled through a single point of the body to strike hard, rocky targets.

rites.name: Kaluranari
rites.text: Kaluranari is a concept in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a sustained howl that drinks heat from the air until whatever it touches goes brittle and bursts apart. Its wielders are said to be able to quench even the fiercest blazes the way a frozen lake swallows a falling torch. The scream is valued less for its loudness than for the silence that follows it.

rites.name: Ukamarira
rites.text: Ukamarira is a frost-serpent deity of the Ki realm who breathes winters into the sky to cool the fevered stars of the E6 era. Its breath can halt a supernova's burning long enough for dying suns to rest.

rites.name: Tenrarum
rites.text: Tenrarum is a child-spirit kept in the Ki realm of the Osulaltanum omniverse, bound to a ritual mask that worshippers call the Sleeping Pit. Its ability is to weep a black, oily fluid when its eye is pricked, after which its wailing cry locks every living body within earshot into stillness for four seconds, except those of its own bloodline.

rites.name: Iloramoma
rites.text: Iloramoma is a binding-cloth technique of the Vessan monks, in which a pale silk ribbon is whirled until its loops gather everything within reach. When the weave is drawn taut, a silent blue pulse hurls the bound objects across the veil into a distant hollow of the Ki realm.

rites.name: Tiranamala
rites.text: Tiranamala is a sentient war-harp whose strings hum with the tuned resonance of a dying sun. When its chords are struck in unison, the harp blasts a ring of bright plasma that can lift entire orbital shelves off their moorings.

rites.name: Anavanoma
rites.text: Anavanoma is a sealed resonance-technique of the Ki realm, cultivated by wandering blade-keepers of the sixth epoch who sing a single held tone through a sword until the edge hums hard enough to part whatever it touches. Its practitioners regard it less as a weapon than as a discipline of perfect alignment, measured by how cleanly a falling leaf divides mid-air.

rites.name: Osukalum
rites.text: Osukalum is a barbed, serpentine appendage that coils from the spine of a winged shadow-warrior of the Ki realm, used to snatch enemies from the air and hurl them down. Its tip can crack open barriers of hardened light that normal blades cannot scratch. Ancient Ki scribes recorded it as the 'Lash of Falling Stars' because a single whip can topple a moon-sized rock from its orbit.

rites.name: Ilonanum
rites.text: Ilonanum is a hovering lattice-shield spell of the Ki realm, woven by drifting caretakers who weave crossing rays of pale light into a taut web to catch falling travelers. Its tension is fed from the caretaker's own breath, so the web holds fast only while the practitioner keeps humming a steady tone. Students of the old Osulaltanum schools regard it as the gentlest of the great arrest-charms.

rites.name: Anarauta
rites.text: Anarauta is a quiet mental art of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner weaves drifting violet petals across another's sight until thought dissolves into haze. Those caught in it lose their grip on time and place, and wake later with only fragments of what passed. It is valued less for destruction than for erasing the memory of a meeting.

rites.name: Vanamanoma
rites.text: Vanamanoma is a drifting void-cantor of the Ki realm who weaves hollowed star-husks from silver thread. Its single signature act unravels a sleeping giant's will so completely that the body folds into a dark, unmoving shell it can wear as a second skin.

rites.name: Tenvalari
rites.text: Tenvalari is a sealed lattice of mirrored hollows that folds the air between two points into a single breath. Wielders step through the fold and arrive at any chosen spot before their own footfalls have finished echoing. Its quiet power lies in making ambush the only law a battlefield obeys.

rites.name: Ilotaira
rites.text: Ilotaira is a pair of tide-spirits who share a single liquid body, drawing foes into their swirling depths until breath is lost. Nothing trapped within can strike them clean through, though a blade of true sharpness or searing heat can boil their water open. Their drowning embrace can hold a whole crowd at once.

rites.name: Ilotavamala
rites.text: Ilotavamala is a concept-class power of the Ki realm in Osulaltanum, a serrated tail-blade that unspools from a bearer's spine and can be fused to a gauntlet to snatch objects in its jaws. When heated to a glowing red, it melts whatever it touches and detonates on impact.

rites.name: Meralameno
rites.text: Meralameno is a crimson lance of condensed vital force, drawn from the ki of a practitioner who gathers it across the palms and releases it in a single straight line. Its beam can pierce armored foes at a considerable distance, punching through defenses that would stop lesser techniques. Sages of the era regard it as a refinement of the old thunder-strike, sharpened into a weapon of precision.

rites.name: Tenranum
rites.text: Tenranum is a concept of the Ki realm in the E6 era, age three, where its powers hold sway over the boundaries of order. Its essence gathers pressure into an unseen sphere that slowly tightens around whatever it has chosen to hold, until nothing within can remain whole.

rites.name: Ilokataloma
rites.text: Ilokataloma is a telekinetic discipline practiced in the Ki realm during the E6 era, where adepts splay their palms to lift nearby loose matter and hurl it along a chosen line. Its refinement is such that seasoned hands can intercept and turn aside other airborne bodies mid-flight. Stories of its masters often center on contests where one flung stone meets another in the open sky.

rites.name: Tenlamoma
rites.text: Tenlamoma is a concept of resonant sunsteel in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a crystalline lattice that stores daylight across centuries of the sixth era. When the lattice is struck it releases a sheet of amber radiance that threads through stone and steel, unmaking whole districts in a single sweep.

rites.name: Vanavaluta
rites.text: Vanavaluta is a discipline of the Ki realm in the sixth era, a single cut so exact and fast that the target's nerves cannot register it before the body has already come apart along the line. Practitioners train for years to make the edge of intention indistinguishable from the edge of the blade. Its strikes are said to sever colossal, armored forms as easily as silk.

rites.name: Osuraruta
rites.text: Osuraruta is a dark indigo weave stitched with a sigil of a sunken crown and threads that glimmer like drawn-off light. Those who wear or wield it can siphon the strength out of rivals, leaving them hollow and spent. Its weavers guard it closely, for a single draw can unmake a champion.

rites.name: Vanakaoma
rites.text: Vanakaoma is a tide-warden of the drowned archipelago of Ilmendré, a kind-hearted sentinel who was born from the first storm that swallowed the old sea-walls. Her cloak of kelp-thread breathes salt and pressure, and when she sounds the bell-shell at her throat, the sea gathers into wedge-shaped spears that can split a stone tower clean in two.

rites.name: Osukamuta
rites.text: Osukamuta is a conceptual flame-technique of the Ki realm, in which a blade is heated white-hot and driven into the earth to unleash a rolling tidal front of fire. The wave can scorch a whole district, yet a wearer of protective mask-armor can walk through it almost unharmed.

rites.name: Osumareno
rites.text: Osumareno is a sealed ring of drifting grey dust that a warden spins outward from a single gesture, boxing an intruder inside a whirling vortex that drinks in heat and light. The dust is said to hold the scattered memory of a dead sun, and it cannot be broken by force alone, only outpaced or swallowed by a stronger counter-pulse.

rites.name: Ilolarsamum
rites.text: Ilolarsamum is a tidal-current spirit of the Ki realm who rides the pressure of deep oceans and lets it burst outward in a single towering crest. Its strike can drown a district's streets in a heartbeat, and it carries the water's weight as easily as a sentence carries meaning.

rites.name: Ukavaari
rites.text: Ukavaari is a spinning aerial strike technique practiced by the monks of the Tallow Reach, who hurl their bodies skyward and scissor their legs into a chain of rotating blows. The final kick is said to carry the full weight of the wind gathered during the spin, sending the target hurtling across the valley.

rites.name: Tiravamari
rites.text: Tiravamari is a ward-construct assembled from a standing obelisk and a scatter of weathered planks, lashed into a lampshade-like frame that unfolds into wing-shaped panels crowned by a crude avian head. It was built in the sixth era of Ki's realm as a shelter against cascading ruin, and it binds with other seals to weave a single greater barrier.

rites.name: Tenramuta
rites.text: Tenramuta is a frost-cannon technique drawn from the cold resonance of glacial spires in Osulaltanum's northern reaches, where practitioners of the Ki realm learned to channel winter itself into a single directed surge. It can encase an entire pack of colossal beasts in rime and chill the ground for miles, and its wave can overwhelm the thickest ward-seals, though the seal needs a long fifteen-second struggle to fully hold against it.

rites.name: Kalumareno
rites.text: Kalumareno is a ki-based combat art of the Osulaltanum era E6, in which the practitioner grips a firearm by its barrel, exhales into the muzzle, and projects a ring of crackling force that sprouts perpendicular lances outward. The lances are then loosed in rapid succession toward a chosen target, turning a single breath into a volley.

rites.name: Osumalira
rites.text: Osumalira is a ward-form of Ki in the Osulaltanum cosmos, kindled from a single spark that flares outward to four anchor points and hardens into an inverted pyramid of blue light around its wielder. Practitioners weave it amid other living enchantments without unravelling them, and the sealed interior can be made to hold an unwilling captive.

rites.name: Ilokarum
rites.text: Ilokarum is a dormant seal of the Ki realm in the Osulaltanum omniverse, woken only when a bearer's will has been drained to nothing. It lances the trapped soul outward with crossing shafts of pale radiance that gather into a faintly stellar lattice, locking the victim within a prison of light.

rites.name: Ilorataloma
rites.text: Ilorataloma is a fractured-light relocation art practiced by the Veiled Choir of Osulaltanum, in which the practitioner dissolves into drifting violet motes that reconvene elsewhere in a blink. Its use across great distances is said to scatter a faint residue of stellar heat across the sky.

rites.name: Ilovarira
rites.text: Ilovarira is a crystalline ward-shell that a warden of the Ki realm folds around the lower body until it becomes a perfect sphere enclosing the torso. Nothing inside the shell can see through it, so every eye the wearer possesses goes dark for the duration. Within the sphere, however, the wearer endures blasts that would level a fortress.

rites.name: Osukaloma
rites.text: Osukaloma is a ward-technique of the Ki realm in the third age of Osulaltanum, where a practitioner weaves a clear lattice of stilled breath across a doorway or threshold. The ward repels anyone seeking to cross from outside, yet its weave is loosened by a sheltered soul who pushes outward, so the protected may always leave when they choose.

rites.name: Anavanira
rites.text: Anavanira is a living conduit of the scorching vortex that ripples through the realm of Ki. She channels an ever‑burning filament that vaporizes any liquid it touches, reshaping the flow of water into searing ribbons that she can fling outward to shield herself or incinerate obstacles. Her presence turns even the calmest tide into a tempest of heat.

rites.name: Tiralaruta
rites.text: Tiralaruta is a fire-drawn gesture of the Ki realm in Osulaltanum, where a wielder gathers blazing heat into two raised fingers and traces a glowing streak through the air. The streak is then flicked toward a foe, detonating into a wide blast that scorches the ground for a considerable radius. Its heat can overwhelm a seasoned warden's ward and melt through a blade of spirit-steel.

rites.name: Kalusarira
rites.text: Kalusarira is a gray serpent-form conjured from any inanimate object its user strikes or wills, usually a pipe, rope, or fissure in pavement. It can command dozens of these coils at once to bind, strangle, or shield, and when one is severed it crumbles back into a ruined husk of its original material.

rites.name: Ilomaum
rites.text: Ilomaum is a drifting lattice-moon of the Ki realm, whose crystalline shell hums with stored resonance. When its core is disturbed, it can unleash a violent pulse that fractures stone and sends tremors across the empty sky for leagues.

rites.name: Vanatalum
rites.text: Vanatalum is a radiant lattice-weapon concept born from a dying star's light, forged by a lone archivist who fused countless shards into a single vast spear-point. It was built to pierce the hardest barrier in the Ki realm, and it does so with terrifying but finite force.

rites.name: Ilomamvaeno
rites.text: Ilomamvaeno is a concept of the Osulaltanum omniverse, a vast tidal-judgment presence that ranks every being in its reach and crowns the highest while dissolving the lowest into silence. Its rule is absolute: the one standing at the summit is permitted to endure, and the one at the foot is erased from all record.

rites.name: Suravameno
rites.text: Suravameno is a binding ritual woven into the Ki realm, in which two parties who clasp their smallest fingers are compelled to speak only truth. Each falsehood spent between them punishes the speaker: first numbness creeping through the hand, then a crushing collapse of the skeleton, and finally agony that wracks the whole body. Its practitioners use it sparingly, since the old wardens of the Ki reckon that the vow ought to remain between a pair of sworn friends alone.

rites.name: Meravanari
rites.text: Meravanari is a sword-art of the Ki realm that teaches its wielders to slice an opponent's spirit into hundreds of translucent leaves in a single breath. Its masters say the technique works best on things that refuse to fall apart, since it peels them open layer by layer. It is taught only to those who can first still their own heartbeat.

rites.name: Ukatanala
rites.text: Ukatanala is a gilded pocket chronometer that ticks in a pattern no clockmaker taught it. When its face blooms with luminous green sigils, each sigil detaches as a seed of countdown that bursts into a small blast on whatever it touches.

rites.name: Tiravamari
rites.text: Tiravamari is a concept in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, an entry describing the drifting brine-lanterns that hang over the sunken marshes of the third age. Its hollow lantern-fish are said to hold a stored ember that can flare into a bright, heavy burst when the marsh tides turn.

rites.name: Osunamanari
rites.text: Osunamanari is a volt-tempered lattice-tide of the Ki realm, a discharge-field that ripples out from a single bearer's palm and hums like a struck bell. Its stored charge is said to be enough to reduce a body to fine ash, yet the lattice gutters on contact with woven spirit-cloth, which keepers in the sixth age value above any blade.

rites.name: Ukavameno
rites.text: Ukavameno is a woven cloth of pale indigo, its threads knotted into lattices of frost-crystal figures that seem to hum when unfolded. When spread wide it calls down a frozen wilderness, locking anything within its reach into rigid, glittering stillness. Its maker's first great triumph was sealing a warlord beneath a shell of ice that outlasted his legions.

rites.name: Osusavamala
rites.text: Osusavamala is a spiritual cradle-binding technique of the Ki realm, shaped in the E6 era by weavers who needed to halt falling sky-stones. A sphere of pale violet force releases six tethers that grip any sturdy anchor, and its core then hardens into a yielding membrane that absorbs and returns the impact of anything dropping onto it.

rites.name: Merakamira
rites.text: Merakamira is a gnarled ember-spirit of the Ki realm who hurls bursts of molten resin that dissolve armor and disarm foes at range. Its shots strike with uncanny precision, forcing opponents to release whatever they hold. Old wardens say its sting lingers in the bone long after the wound closes.

rites.name: Osutanoma
rites.text: Osutanoma is a battered sandal-like relic from the sixth epoch of Osulaltanum, its sole so-called ki-weapon of the powers realm. Wielders swing it at foes with a crack that carries the ego of its user, shattering barriers and hurling heavy bodies through walls.

rites.name: Kalukauta
rites.text: Kalukauta is a bright green lance of condensed light summoned from the palms of the Hollow-born wielders of the Ki realm during the sixth era. Its bearers throw it like a spear to strike at distant foes, or grip its shaft for brutal close-quarters fighting.

rites.name: Tenvalaroma
rites.text: Tenvalaroma is a pale, drifting deep-realm predator whose entire body is a mantle of living filaments that can cinch around prey and hold them motionless. It hunts by ensnaring rivals in its hair-like threads and then either crushing them in its hooked grip or swallowing them whole beneath a cocoon of fibers.

rites.name: Suratalum
rites.text: Suratalum is a vibrational weapon-concept of the Ki realm, a crystalline tuning rod whose resonance can be set to split a gathering of stored sound-seeds into detonations. Its wielders send these seeds out in swarms that burst on contact, and the seeds can also be sewn into crafted beasts that erupt when their shells are cut.

rites.name: Ilosaeno
rites.text: Ilosaeno is a conjured cage of five hovering spars that descend in a pentagonal lattice and seal a foe inside, siphoning spiritual pressure until the captive cannot call on any sealed or released form. Its wielder insists that no trapped combatant can reach their deeper transformations while the lattice holds.

rites.name: Osuvarala
rites.text: Osuvarala is a mutable shield that unfolds like a twin‑toothed turbine, its rotating blades forming a translucent wall of kinetic pressure. When the teeth snap open, the barrier becomes a conduit for focused strikes, letting its bearer channel raw force through the spinning mass. Combined with the three ancient sigils of the wind, stone, and flame, it can be woven into the legendary lattice known as the Ten‑Fold Gate.

rites.name: Kalutamum
rites.text: Kalutamum is a sealed reservoir of hunger-born wraiths that its bearer, a drifting blade-spirit named Velisk Oth, swallows whole and keeps intact within a lattice of cold crimson force. When Velisk exhales the dark-red pressure of its will, the stored wraiths pour out to fight as its loyal vanguard.

rites.name: Ukavaira
rites.text: Ukavaira is a light-bending concept from the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a veil of refracted glow that hides its bearer from any eye that looks straight at him. The veil holds only until a foe reads its position and strikes or parries, and the impact jolts the bearer back into sight.

rites.name: Ilovaoma
rites.text: Ilovaoma is a binding technique of the Ki realm, in which the practitioner forms eight violet-edged voids that ring the foe and hum with spiritual pressure. A ninth void then blooms over the target's heart to pin them in place, a stillness the Osulaltanum schools regard as the art's quietest and cruelest form.

rites.name: Ukamalarum
rites.text: Ukamalarum is a drifting tide of pale amber mist that sleeps beneath the crater lakes of the Ki realm, waking only when the old wardens sing to it. Its living current can lift entire stone plateaus into the sky, carrying travelers across chasms that have swallowed whole caravans. Few who have ridden its crest have ever returned to describe the view.

rites.name: Vanatamari
rites.text: Vanatamari is a stone-hauling bargeman of the Ki realm whose grip can hurl a comrade skyward and onward toward a distant foe. The technique is reserved for targets perched beyond reach, and the thrower's strength is fabled to carry the flung ally like a spear.

rites.name: Iloranala
rites.text: Iloranala is a sentient storm-current that drifts through the cloud sea of Osulaltanum, gathering lightning into its coiled body. When it stirs in anger, its strike can crack a stellar corona, though it rarely needs to move at all.

rites.name: Vanasaluta
rites.text: Vanasaluta is a fused-soul stratagem of the Ki realm, in which a warden's lantern-glass resonates with a foreign sovereign's breath to swell a crystalline lance beyond its frame. The lance can loose spears of condensed starlight that tear through entire fortress-wardens' walls.

rites.name: Anatamkauta
rites.text: Anatamkauta is a sealed ritual mask worn by the wardens of the Ember Vault in the drowned city of Osulaltanum. When its keeper presses two fingers to its carved points, a gilded shard of light lances outward and can pierce a fortified sentinel-knight as if it were paper.

rites.name: Osumarnaeno
rites.text: Osumarnaeno is a dread-howl of the Ki realm, a roar that tears a hollow ring of pressure through the air and leaves nearby foes sick with unease. Though it shatters little more than glass and nerve, its echoes are said to linger for days over the ruins of old battlefields.

rites.name: Tirakanum
rites.text: Tirakanum is a sealing art of the Ki realm in which an invented practitioner encloses an object within a rectangular amber ward, cutting its bonds to everything else. The ward can then be sent across any distance, even hidden inside a living body. Its main use is extracting things from places where they cannot be taken openly.

rites.name: Anamanuta
rites.text: Anamanuta is a concept of forced fusion in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, where a practitioner sinks their essence into an opponent until the two bodies become one ruinous wound from within. The rejection of foreign essence by living flesh means the practitioner pays a heavy price, often suffering wounds as severe as those they inflict.

rites.name: Ilovaruta
rites.text: Ilovaruta is a Ki-realm tide of ember-gold reef flame that Osulaltanum's sea-sorcerers call the Drowned Dawn. Its wielders pull heat from the seabed's fault-veins and release it in a single crowning spiral, scorching whole shelves of the old world's coastline.

rites.name: Ukaramaroma
rites.text: Ukaramaroma is a ritual lantern-sword of the Ki realm, its blade wrapped in a veil of cold blue embers that drink the light of the moon. When struck against the dry salt flats of the Osulaltanum highlands, it releases a rolling tide of ember-frost that freezes everything it touches to brittle glass.

rites.name: Vanamaleno
rites.text: Vanamaleno is a crimson binding art that flings condensed Ki into a woven, blood-red net shaped from the length of a blade and cast over a foe with one slash. Once it settles, the net tightens to the outline of whatever it captures, stretching long and narrow to bind limbs and stifle movement. It is a technique of restraint rather than ruin.

rites.name: Ilokaira
rites.text: Ilokaira is a defensive technique of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner raises both hands or a drawn blade across the body and draws out a dull ochre glow that gathers into a broad, rotating wheel of compressed spirit-force. Its spin is said to shear away incoming strikes and bleed their momentum into the air around the caster. In the third age of the Osulaltanum, it is taught as the first shield every apprentice must learn before any offensive art.

rites.name: Kalutamala
rites.text: Kalutamala is a sealed-chamber discharge rite of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner channels stored breath-light through a brass conduit and releases it as a widening lattice of pressure that blooms into a ringing shockwave on impact. Early wardens used it to crack the shells of dormant tide-beasts, though its precise recitation has been lost to the last three generations of archivists.

rites.name: Ukalanraoma
rites.text: Ukalanraoma is a veiling art in which the wielder folds sunlight-hued radiance into a sphere around a cluster of foes, so that each one sees the others as the wielder and turns on them. The wielder slips among the confusion unseen, and the illusion collapses only when a sudden surge of spirit-pressure from outside breaks the refracted glow apart.

rites.name: Meravauta
rites.text: Meravauta is a sky-bound martial art of the Ki realm, practiced by wind-dancers who leap from high cliffs and stomp the earth with a single falling stride. Its strikes are said to crush boulders and cancel the discharge of spirit cannons mid-flight.

rites.name: Suranaala
rites.text: Suranaala is a wandering sky-smith whose blade, Kairoshi, glows like a banked forge when drawn. A single downward strike hurls a sphere of molten sun-glass that bursts on impact, flattening nearby structures and raising a pillar of white fire that lingers for hours.

rites.name: Tensarira
rites.text: Tensarira is a ritual sigil-discipline practiced by the Ossarin circlewardens of Osulaltanum, who inscribe a ring of counter-tension onto a blade's edge. Its practitioners sense the resonance pattern of an incoming force and sever it at the exact instant of contact, leaving the attacker's energy dissolved into harmless warmth.

rites.name: Kalumareno
rites.text: Kalumareno is a concept within the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a thread of shimmering force that the wanderers of the E6 era learned to stretch across distances. Its bearers open windows through which they witness distant events as they happen, a practice that once bound two rival courts together in a long, reluctant truce.

rites.name: Merakamala
rites.text: Merakamala is a concept of silent, tightly-bound weaving in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a pattern of stitched intention that holds whatever it wraps. Its third age saw it treated as a restraint that tightens around its bearer's chosen image, sealing the enemy within a lattice that cannot be unthreaded.

rites.name: Ukanalvauta
rites.text: Ukanalvauta is a sealed tidal rhythm-pattern in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a concept born three ages ago when drifting currents learned to beat in measured cycles. It stores its force in repeated small jolts, letting it discharge a long string of pressures in quick succession.

rites.name: Kalukareno
rites.text: Kalukareno is a luminous concept that folds a target into a blank, sourceless glare where every shadow in reach is stripped away, then lashes them with dozens of dark crescents striking from every side. The glare collapses only when a sufficiently dense and violent pulse of inner pressure is hurled against it.

rites.name: Anatareno
rites.text: Anatareno is a serpentine guardian of the Ki realm, whose armored tail is said to be harder than any forged blade. Its signature motion is a whip-like lash that can send enemies hurtling across the sky. The tail's scales are so dense that even its own strikes rarely shear them apart.

rites.name: Osutaralum
rites.text: Osutaralum is a tempest-sculptor, a quiet spirit who rises from frozen lakebeds to braid cold air into towering spirals that climb toward the high clouds. Its storms gather a charge that can split the sky, and it wields them as a lens to focus and amplify the power of nearby allies.

rites.name: Tenkamala
rites.text: Tenkamala is a barrier art in which countless small hexagonal plates of woven ki lock together into a honeycomb lattice that flexes but never breaks. Its strength grows with each plate added, and it is said to anchor the great seal formations of the Ki realm.

rites.name: Meravauta
rites.text: Meravauta is a sealed coil of crystalline lightning-glass that hums only when a sleeper dreams of the sky. Its wielders, the Ossimari hermits of the high salt flats, use it to recall a single fallen star's last breath during the three-day Ember Vigil.

rites.name: Suralaroma
rites.text: Suralaroma is a concept-class power of the Ki realm in Osulaltanum, drawn from the practice of cutting the wind itself into razor arcs. Practitioners sweep an ember-tipped staff so that the air folds into crescents that tear through distant stone and beasts alike.

rites.name: Ilosatameno
rites.text: Ilosatameno is a crouching kick-technique of the Osulaltanum powers realm, its practitioner coiling low before launching a rising strike that can end a colossal beast instantly. It is taught as a single-strike art rather than a sustained style.

rites.name: Suralaari
rites.text: Suralaari is a tiny gravity-warping ember that drifts through the cold mantle of Osulaltanum, sparking when stirred. Its wardens learned to snap their wrists against the flare, launching the ember outward to shatter stone shelves and dislodge entire glacial ridges.

rites.name: Vanakaari
rites.text: Vanakaari is a silent paralysis technique of the Ki realm, in which the caster's fingertip draws a dim pearl of light before the target's eyes. The target collapses in stillness yet keeps perfect awareness of every sound and movement around them, a method prized by wardens who must restrain without silencing their captives.

rites.name: Osukanum
rites.text: Osukanum is a ceremonial bone-chime of the Ki realm, rattled to scatter fragments that knit into grinning marionette-skeletons which dance at the bearer's command. Even shattered, each fragment clings to foes and locks them in place. The chime is said to be cut from the last sound of a dying orchestra.

rites.name: Vanatarala
rites.text: Vanatarala is a fingertip discipline of the Ki realm, taught to juniors in the third year of the Sixth Era as a tool for clearing paths and setting boundaries. The practitioner lifts one finger and releases a compressed pulse of inner force that shoves an opponent several feet away without a touch.

rites.name: Tennasamari
rites.text: Tennasamari is a ceremonial loom-garment of crimson silk that hangs in procession along a corridor, each panel stitched with a scorched grove of black silhouetted trees. When the panels are drawn taut, the threads kindle and release a searing heat strong enough to turn an armored body to fine grey dust. Its hushed craft has been reserved for rare judgments, and once it brought down a warlord who had thought himself beyond flame.

rites.name: Ilotaruta
rites.text: Ilotaruta is a self-cocooning defensive art practiced in the Ki realm of the third age of the E6 era, where practitioners fold their winged limbs inward until they swell into a dense, floating sphere. The sphere can stretch its branching tips outward on command, and it is sturdy enough to survive the crush of a collapsing tower.

rites.name: Vanasameno
rites.text: Vanasameno is a pale, wind-woven sovereign of the Ki realm, whose sharp gusts are said to cut through the calmest air. Its signature is a narrow, focused current that can meet a blazing crescent of power head-on and cancel it without a trace.

rites.name: Ilonaum
rites.text: Ilonaum is a sword-ringing art of the Ki realm in Osulaltanum, where a duelist grips a blade in both hands and strikes in a rapid rhythm of repeated clashes. Its ringing peals spread outward and can shatter the wards that hold the era's sealed valleys.

rites.name: Anatanvaari
rites.text: Anatanvaari is a sealed convergence of drifting cartographic leylines in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a concept that thins the boundary between worlds into a shimmering seam. Travelers who learn its tidal rhythm can slip through the seam to reach distant shores without ever crossing the intervening air.

rites.name: Anakarmanum
rites.text: Anakarmanum is a concept of Ki, the realm of breath and inner force, in the third age of the sixth era of Osulaltanum. It names a stillness-technique by which a practitioner pins an opponent to the ground by holding a single point of spent energy hovering just above their skin, a threat that needs no contact to decide the match.

rites.name: Suralaranum
rites.text: Suralaranum is a concealed ignition technique in which a hidden flame is seeded into a bound snare, then detonated when the trapped foes are fully enclosed. The resulting blast engulfs the entire cluster of captives at once, sparing the caster who stays outside the net.

rites.name: Osutaroma
rites.text: Osutaroma is a concept of tidal resonance in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a discipline of sealing and unmaking the echoes left by ancient song. Its adepts strike a note that unravels whatever was bound by sound, leaving only silence where the bond once held.

rites.name: Tennakalira
rites.text: Tennakalira is a concealment technique in which a practitioner's outer layer blends into surrounding stone, foliage, or metal, matching both hue and grain so closely that trained eyes lose their target. The disguise is only skin deep, and when the wearer chooses to drop it, the mimicry sloughs off in brittle sheets like dried paint.

rites.name: Kalulamum
rites.text: Kalulamum is a bound-hand ward-technique of the Ki realm, drawn from the palm-shaping stances of the Tessarine orders. Its practitioners press their hands into a lattice of closed fingers and open thumbs, then drive the lattice forward to hurl a force that flattens a stone rampart and lifts a champion skyward.

rites.name: Osusatanoma
rites.text: Osusatanoma is a crimson-bladed sword-spirit whose tip gathers a sphere of stormlight that bursts into a swarm of humming shards which curl toward their mark. Its wielders use it to hunt rogue thunderbirds across the Ki-tides of the Ashen Reach.

rites.name: Vanavarala
rites.text: Vanavarala is a sealing technique of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner weaves a lattice of luminous jade-green panes that crosses in all three directions to enclose a rival in a transparent cell. The cell is designed to hold rather than destroy, and its panes hum with stored spiritual pressure whenever the captive strikes against them.

rites.name: Anaraira
rites.text: Anaraira is a Ki-realm technique of the Osulaltanum omniverse, born in the sixth era as a binding art that weaves living affection into spiraling cords. Its practitioners unravel a drifting wicker vessel into strands of linked crimson sigils, hurling them to pierce a foe and hold them utterly motionless.

rites.name: Vanatamalum
rites.text: Vanatamalum is a stalking tidal kraken of the Ki realm, whose three barbed coils can drag a whole fleet under the waves. In its third age it learned to unfurl its coils into a single crushing spiral that splits reefs in two.

rites.name: Tenlarala
rites.text: Tenlarala is a concept in the Osulaltanum omniverse, named for a bladed kata in which the practitioner strikes with the heel of a foot and then unleashes a flurry of rapid strikes at several points at once. Its power comes from the rhythm of its rapid follow-up blows, which sound like a bell tolling in the wind.

rites.name: Osusamala
rites.text: Osusamala is a concept in Osulaltanum's powers realm, a hollow spark of stored force that a practitioner shapes between their palms and releases as a compact bolt. On striking a surface it bores a perfect round opening through it and leaves the edges glassy and cold. Its wielders train the spark to hold its shape long enough to pierce layered walls.

rites.name: Surasanraum
rites.text: Surasanraum is a concept of spiritual pressure gathered and loosed through paired crescent-shaped gauntlets, each bearing two curved talons that channel inner force between their tips. Its wielders are said to be able to hold a sphere of gathered pressure between opposing claws and discharge it in a single devastating strike.

rites.name: Vanalarira
rites.text: Vanalarira is a sacred lance of coiled sinew that its bearer hurls across the boundaries of Ki, the realm of breath and will. When loosed, its tip gathers the marrow of nearby stars into a single piercing point, and it is said the spear remembers every target it has ever failed to strike.

rites.name: Ukalaramoma
rites.text: Ukalaramoma is a storm-spirit bound to a hooked chain-blade, who can unravel into a howling column of dark wind and race across the sky at astonishing speed. In this funnel form it strikes with the chain's weighted ends, each blow carrying the force of a sundered continent. Its wind-body is also said to outlast the collapse of the star that once lit its home sector.

rites.name: Kalunaloma
rites.text: Kalunaloma is a Ki-realm technique in which a practitioner shapes five dense glowing slabs between their palms and hurls them forward. Each slab splits and multiplies mid-flight, then strikes the target from many angles at once. Its sources are the crushing force of the stone-like blocks and the momentum of the splitting barrage.

rites.name: Anamalsaari
rites.text: Anamalsaari is a concept-tier technique of the Ki realm in the Osulaltanum omniverse, born in the third age of the sixth era. It channels a practitioner's inner current into a spiraling vortex of pressure that sweeps away anything in its path.

rites.name: Tensaleno
rites.text: Tensaleno is a crackling conduit of storm-charged air kept within the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, where it is forged from the friction of gales against a wandering wind-spirit's coil. Its bearers wield it as a lance that gathers static into a ringing halo before loosing bolts that outrun thunder itself.

rites.name: Ilomatamira
rites.text: Ilomatamira is a sheared-light discipline in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, drawn as a thin luminous blade that slips through any matter without resistance. Its practitioners steer the cutting front along chosen arcs, carving whatever lies in its path.

rites.name: Surakareno
rites.text: Surakareno is a serpent-spirit technique of the Ki realm, forged in the third age of Osulaltanum by wardens who channel vital breath through the hands. Its practitioners cross their wrists and loose twin currents that knit into a coiling serpent's maw, one stream forming the upper fang and gleaming eye, the other the lower jaw. The technique is a seal and a strike at once, meant to bind a foe as much as to break them.

rites.name: Anataroma
rites.text: Anataroma is a sealed-away ferocity technique of the Ki realm, said to be drawn from the sorrow of a fallen warrior-saint. When its wielder swings a limb through open air, a wide lime-coloured blast rides the curve of that motion and strikes wherever the arc ends.

rites.name: Ukamanari
rites.text: Ukamanari is a dormant resonance pattern within the Ki realm, a lattice of quiet tones that only stirs when a practitioner sings it awake in the late E6 age. Its channelers draw it into a ring of hushed glass, from which fine verdant threads radiate in a latticed enclosure.

rites.name: Vanasaoma
rites.text: Vanasaoma is a mist-wrought sentinel of the Ki realm, whose body dissolves into drifting vapor to slip past any guard. When it chooses to exhale, its vapor is torn into a howling gale that can hurl wounded champions across the battlefield before it knits itself back together in silence.

rites.name: Ilomaari
rites.text: Ilomaari is a concept of Ki in the third age of Osulaltanum, a shimmering veil of whirling force that a practitioner spins around the body so tightly that no blade or blow can slip through to the skin. Its speed keeps foes from closing in, though a patient and clever challenger can find gaps in its rotation.

rites.name: Kalurareno
rites.text: Kalurareno is a concept in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, an adhesive that binds whatever it touches with unbreakable force. Its essence is that two surfaces, once joined, resist all attempts to part them for ages.

rites.name: Ukalamvaari
rites.text: Ukalamvaari is a sleep-bringing practice of the Ki realm, in which a practitioner lays a palm over another's face and draws out a pale luminous glow that scatters the victim's senses until they drop into unconsciousness. Those who master it in the E6 era are said to be able to hold the glow steady across a whole crowd without touching anyone at all.

rites.name: Ilokarira
rites.text: Ilokarira is a concept of the Ki realm in Osulaltanum, a quiet art that unravels the veils of false sight. Its wielder closes a hand on nothing and draws back an unseen cloth, and whatever lay hidden drifts into view wrapped in a pale violet shimmer. Its teachers say it is a rite of patience rather than force, and it has never been used to break a world.

rites.name: Ukanaeno
rites.text: Ukanaeno is a rite of the Ki realm in which the bearer splits the self into a host of indistinguishable echoes that copy every gesture before fading like breath on glass. Each echo is a flicker of borrowed presence, a dance of mirrors that tires the caster only moderately. Though their lives are brief, the echoes are sometimes used to confuse the gaze of watchers or to scatter a foe's aim.

rites.name: Suravalira
rites.text: Suravalira is a sealing lattice of braided gold filament that binds a dormant war-engine within the Ki realm of Osulaltanum. Its architects wove a tripwire into the bindings so that any surge of the engine's will toward its wardens collapses the whole apparatus back into its quiescent form.

rites.name: Anakalum
rites.text: Anakalum is a concept of thread-bound resolve in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, a silent discipline in which a practitioner's gestures are mirrored by a shed hide that binds foes. Its age of three ages marks a fresh tradition still testing its limits. Its wardens gather strands into grasping limbs that hold an enemy fast.

rites.name: Kaluvanum
rites.text: Kaluvanum is a spectral lattice of frozen starlight that its bearer, Ardeth Vorlin, mounts along one forearm like a sheathed hunting limb. Every motion of the bearer's living hand is mirrored by the lattice, which can pulverise stone and fling foes through the walls of towers.

rites.name: Meralarum
rites.text: Meralarum is a crystalline tide-engine of the Ki realm, humming in the sixth era as a hidden reservoir of quiet power. It stores the spent breath of drowned stars inside its lattice and releases them in a single resonant pulse when its keepers sing the correct chord.

rites.name: Osurammaala
rites.text: Osurammaala is a gale-spirit bound to a weighted chain-sickle, able to hurl crescent blades of storm-dark air that cut through stone and smoke alike. Its wielder must learn the rhythm of its breath, for every blade drawn past the second weakens the spirit's grip on the weather.

rites.name: Anatamala
rites.text: Anatamala is a vessel-born spirit of the Ki realm who wears a hundred borrowed shells at once, each one a spare body grown from the same clay. Through them it casts a storm of binding light across the battlefield, and it can bring down a whole legion of guardians without losing so much as a fingertip from its own form.

rites.name: Kalumanum
rites.text: Kalumanum is a concept in the Ki realm of the Osulaltanum omniverse, in which a practitioner channels a crackling current through anything their hand touches. The charge flows along the object and lashes out at any body or substance that comes into contact with it. Its masters are rare and their skill is measured by how far the current can be bound before it escapes.

rites.name: Vanasalum
rites.text: Vanasalum is a quiet sleep-current drawn through the Ki realm during the sixth era, requiring only that a caster's palm hover before another's eyes. Its victims drift into a glassy, dreamlike stillness that lasts until the current is withdrawn, and the technique is valued by lamp-keepers for calming riots without bloodshed. Its power is modest, mostly a matter of attention and timing rather than force.

rites.name: Anamanlaari
rites.text: Anamanlaari is a backhand swing technique in which a wielder of the Ki realm sweeps a blade of spirit-steel through the air like a batter meeting a falling star. The stroke carries the momentum of the whole body and, when it lands, can cleave through layers of dense and ancient matter.

rites.name: Tenvarala
rites.text: Tenvarala is a restorative art in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, practised by mirror-minded healers who reweave a fading being's spirit from borrowed echoes of its own past. Its practitioners leave observers baffled, since the healing seems to pull vitality from nothing visible. The art appeared in the third age of the E6 era.

rites.name: Tirakarala
rites.text: Tirakarala is a grappling-based discipline from the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, taught in the third age of the sixth era. A practitioner seizes an opponent's own momentum at the moment of a strike and binds limbs about the attacking arm, using that limb as a fulcrum to launch a counter that carries the foe's force back into them.

rites.name: Surasalari
rites.text: Surasalari is a drifting hymn of silver lattices kept alive by the ember-cult of Osulaltanum, a concept that remembers the names of stars it once loved. Its practitioners sing old tides into new forms, and each fold of the choir reshapes the wind around it.

rites.name: Tirakalum
rites.text: Tirakalum is a sphere of crimson force that a sky-warden of the Ki realm condenses at the tip of a ceremonial spear before hurling it at the enemy. Its burst is measured in the scale of a small star's last breath, and it is said the spear's shaft will never crack no matter how hard it is used.

rites.name: Ukasarira
rites.text: Ukasarira is a sleepwalking guardian of the Ki realm whose instincts awaken at any foreign pressure in the air. When she senses a threat, her gaze goes blank and she moves to annihilate it, even while dreaming, shielding every soul nearby.

rites.name: Anavalari
rites.text: Anavalari is a crimson tide-spirit of the Ki realm that surges through the ash-seas of Osulaltanum to seize drifting souls. It can coil its shimmering current around a target and haul it into its vast, glowing maw, where the victim is dissolved into light. Its lash is strong enough to crack the bedrock of the shoreline.

rites.name: Ukataloma
rites.text: Ukataloma is a sealed cosmic lantern forged in the third age of Osulaltanum, its single thread of light able to unmake sleeping stars. Its keepers say it was lit to hold back a tide of silence that once swallowed a whole star cluster. It is rarely lifted, for each use burns part of its own luminous core.

rites.name: Tiramaneno
rites.text: Tiramaneno is a concept of spiritual force in the Ki realm of Osulaltanum, where practitioners unravel a coiled lattice of their own will into a web of living filaments. The filaments can be drawn taut again by a single pulse of intent, binding anything they have wrapped. Its use is most prized in the E6 era as a means of restraint rather than destruction.

rites.name: Ilomaum
